assertion.objects: The fixed-type maximal-O CM class orbit, selected O-stable cyclic N-level subgroup and the actual reduction place at the odd inert prime q.
assertion.hypotheses: O is maximal with units plus or minus one in the conductor-one use; q is odd inert and unramified; N is prime to q*disc(F) and split prime by prime; preserve the fixed type and labelled O action.
assertion.quantifiers: Every ideal class and each finite diagram of selected prime-to-Nq ideal isogenies.
assertion.parameter_range: Arbitrary split prime-power level, including powers of two; q=3 allowed.
assertion.uniformity: One common finite extension for each finite diagram; no uniform field for all torsion or all diagrams.
assertion.constants: The actual degree Norm(a) and unaveraged class sum; no class-number division.
assertion.normalizations: The quotient acts by a^-1 on lattices. A global inversion of all Artin labels leaves the quadratic class sum unchanged; no independent per-class or per-place inversion.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The enhanced geometric target torsor, rational embedding/local order calculation and final analytic weight transformations remain separate. No general nonmaximal-order or conductor-changing CJ theorem follows.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the type, selected level and place, construct the finite diagram and common models, then specialize and compare the same ideal action.

assertion.statement: The two local coefficient-recovery arguments invert the specified integer quadratic substitution and bounded-step integer affine change after a bounded nonzero multiplier.

assertion.normalizations: Integer multipliers clear the modular coefficient ambiguities before inversion.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An O(X) translation is retained in weighted coefficient bookkeeping; unbounded affine step is excluded.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the substitution bounds and degree before varying X.

assertion.parameter_range: All integer exponents, all real coordinate parameters, all permitted finite alphabet sizes, including zero survivors.

assertion.statement: Basic group commutators give integer normal forms in free nilpotent groups, and their fixed-length classes form a free abelian lower-central basis. This yields integral Hall coordinates, lattices, and exact lattice intersections for the upward-closed monomial quotients used here.
assertion.objects: Free nilpotent group of class m, associated graded Lie ring, free real Lie algebra, finite Hall list, discrete group Lambda generated by exp letters.
assertion.hypotheses: Finite ordered alphabet; nilpotency class at most m. Uniqueness and graded independence are used only for the free group. Additional relations are exactly sums of upward-closed individual-letter multidegrees.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such quotient and every further upward-closed homogeneous subgroup S.
assertion.parameter_range: All integer exponents, all real coordinate parameters, all permitted finite alphabet sizes, including zero survivors.
assertion.uniformity: Coordinate maps, lattices and fundamental sets depend only on the fixed Hall list and the forbidden multidegrees.
assertion.constants: The coordinate inverse is a finite triangular polynomial; compact representatives use [0,1]^v. No unspecified finite computation is used.
assertion.normalizations: Tointon weight is bracket length; manuscript weight w is a separate positive grading. The ordered group-commutator coordinate need not be a single homogeneous Lie word.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Discarded Hall factors vanish including their BCH corrections. Saturation is proved for these monomial ideals, not asserted for arbitrary rational quotients.
assertion.limit_order: Integral coordinate proof is over standard real groups before any ultrapower.

use.reason: The actual bad-word ideal is upward closed at every weight. Apply the integral Hall-coordinate lemma to this monomial quotient, then use the separately supplied real annihilation for the character. Lattice saturation does not itself prove real character vanishing.

assertion.quantifiers: Every x in L0 for one D chosen from the finitely many coordinate polynomials of this fixed construction.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed finite-dimensional nilpotent groups and fixed rational bases; no varying-family denominator estimate.
assertion.uniformity: The same D works for all integer coordinate vectors x in L0 within this fixed construction.
assertion.constants: D is a common positive multiple of coordinate-polynomial denominators and the prior BCH denominator requirement.

assertion.limit_order: Fix rho and bases; write the finite rational coordinate polynomials; choose one common multiple D; then evaluate on every integer vector. Increasing D preserves denominator divisibility.

assertion.statement: The exact lower-degree representation transfers to limit data, and precomposition with any fixed integer homomorphism preserves the degree bound and yields the original symbol equality.
assertion.objects: Fixed quotient K/H_s and its lattice, limit polynomial P, bounded Lipschitz limit test function, homomorphism (L1,L1prime,L2,...,Ls).
assertion.hypotheses: Original structural data are standard; F is a bounded Lipschitz limit function with a standard vertical character; coefficients may be limit coefficients.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such limit family and every fixed tuple of homomorphisms; the defining unit-norm and vertical identities quantify over all limit points and all limit top-group elements. Standard-point-only identities do not imply the exact transfer used here.
assertion.parameter_range: All integer inputs; arbitrary standard s,m>=1.
assertion.uniformity: The same quotient and metric constants for all members; no choice of a new nilmanifold from each large coefficient.
assertion.constants: Exact representation, no correlation loss, approximation error or norm rescaling.
assertion.normalizations: Symbol relation is lower-degree tensor quotient, with the two required conjugations.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Limit representatives may be restricted to an ultrafilter-large set on which the exact defining identities hold.
assertion.limit_order: Fix structural data, normalize each polynomial within one compact set, use the uniform geometric construction, and then take the limit.

assertion.statement: Positive binomial coefficient estimates transfer through a bounded-step integer affine map with an O(N) offset after one standard denominator multiplier.
assertion.objects: Real horizontal polynomial f, transformed polynomial f(A+bm), positive binomial coefficients and their circle norms.
assertion.hypotheses: One variable, fixed degree, nonzero bounded integer b, |A|=O(N), transformed positive degree-j coefficient O(N^-j) modulo integers.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such internal polynomial and progression, with one standard multiplier for all positive coefficients.
assertion.parameter_range: k=1 in the general MF-AFFINE lemma; dense progression length comparable to N in DF002.
assertion.uniformity: Denominator depends on fixed degree and bounded step, not the offset or integer parts of coefficients.
assertion.constants: Inverse coefficient from degree j to positive degree i is O(N^(j-i)); residual O(N^-j) therefore gives O(N^-i).
assertion.normalizations: Clear the common rational denominator before reducing modulo integers; no bound is required for degree zero.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Negative nonzero b is allowed; multiplying the nonzero horizontal character by a positive standard integer preserves nonzeroness.
assertion.limit_order: Fix geometry, degree and progression step bound; choose the standard denominator multiplier; transfer all positive estimates simultaneously.

assertion.statement: The same-field maximal-order CM factor Eprime has original stable height equal to the average of -log(2pi)-2log|eta(tau)|-(1/2)log Im(tau) after a good-reduction extension.
assertion.objects: The actual Eprime/L from the maximal-order quotient, with fundamental discriminant Delta_F; its individual complex embeddings.
assertion.hypotheses: Eprime is a CM elliptic curve, hence potentially everywhere good; the analytic discriminant formula applies to each embedding and the finite discriminant term vanishes on the good-reduction extension.
assertion.quantifiers: Every embedding of a field where Eprime has everywhere good reduction; average with division by its absolute degree.
assertion.parameter_range: CM elliptic curves over number fields, with reduced imaginary-quadratic periods.
assertion.uniformity: Stable height is unchanged by the auxiliary good-reduction extension, whose degree never enters the later isogeny bound.
assertion.constants: Analytic discriminant (2pi)^12 eta(tau)^24; sqrt(3)/2<=Im(tau)<=sqrt(|Delta_F|)/2.
assertion.normalizations: Original stable Faltings metric; individual-embedding equation6.2, not the class-average Proposition6.1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No Weierstrass-coefficient condition over Q(j) is imported from Proposition6.1; the auxiliary good-reduction field is not the isogeny field L.
assertion.limit_order: Construct Eprime over L, pass to a good-reduction extension only to evaluate stable height, apply the individual formula, and return to the same L for the isogeny estimate.

preliminary_derivation.argument: If A were geometrically simple, its division endomorphism algebra acts faithfully on H1 of dimension4 and its dimension divides4. Containing B forces equality with B, which lacks a commutative semisimple subalgebra of dimension4 required by CM type. Distinct elliptic factors give a product of commutative fields, incompatible with B. A non-CM repeated factor gives M2(Q), which cannot be isomorphic to division B.

assertion.hypotheses: The rational Gamma_H model, newform-quotient differential description, actual realization of r_ell in A_f and Tate restriction for A are supplied. A is absolutely simple. Faltings Hom comparison, rational scalar extension and Poincare reducibility are retained.
assertion.quantifiers: The same final primitive form after twisting, including every Galois conjugate of its differential; the same Lprime used for actual Tate restriction.
assertion.parameter_range: Arbitrary weight-two nebentypus and coefficient degree; H contains−1.
assertion.uniformity: No coefficient-field degree or extra cyclotomic extension is introduced.
assertion.constants: g=dim J_H≥2. The quotient identities use |H_eff|, not a duplicated central−1 factor.
assertion.normalizations: q e_H=q follows from all conjugate differentials. Use pi-star pi-push=sum over effective H, and pi-push pi-star=[|H_eff|]; averages over H and H_eff agree. The source Jacobian has its canonical principal polarization.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No bounded polarization degree for A or Z is assumed. No use of an ineffective H sum as the quotient degree. The actual representation inclusion and Faltings theorem remain separate inputs.
assertion.limit_order: Construct rational quotient; descend the newform quotient through the effective projector; obtain the constituent in J_H; compare actual Tate modules over Lprime; apply Hom and reducibility.

assertion.statement: The same full-marking scheme Y_Q is the entire canonical principal-level U(3) Shimura curve, with maximal-level forgetful map and canonical normalizer action; its generic coarse degree is36.
assertion.objects: All arithmetic components of Y_Q, the quaternionic type-C1 rational Hodge datum and full finite-adelic U(3) marking orbit.
assertion.hypotheses: The full representable marking scheme and its universal surface are supplied; the exact Milne Hodge-orbit, algebraic family, canonical-model and uniqueness criteria and the integral principal-polarization assertion are retained.
assertion.quantifiers: Every component and every marked geometric object of the full functor, compatibly with all automorphisms of C/Q.
assertion.parameter_range: Discriminant210, principal full level3, reflex fieldQ; both real half-planes and all unit marking multipliers.
assertion.uniformity: The comparison is for the entire Q-model and commutes with level forgetting and normalizer action.
assertion.constants: Stack degree72 and generic coarse degree36 after quotienting central signs; no extra field or level introduced.
assertion.normalizations: Compatible alternating forms have a full Q-times similitude class. The actual positive polarization representative is chosen only at the integral-object stage. Galois comparison uses algebraic torsion data, not rational Betti cohomology.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No uncorrected general implication from Milne8.14/8.17; verify the type-C1 full Hodge orbit directly. No positive-multiplier subgroup or fixed mod3 pairing value is substituted. CM and reciprocity ancestry of the canonical criterion remains a source input.
assertion.limit_order: Verify compatible forms and full Hodge orbit; match integral Tate lattices through finite torsion quotients; construct algebraic families and markings on every component; apply the exact canonical Q-model criterion and uniqueness.

assertion.uniformity: One representable full functor on arbitrary bases, not a chosen component or merely geometric-point classification.

assertion.objects: The quaternion algebra B/Q=End^0_Qbar(A), abstract quadratic F and specified embeddings i:F→B and j=f^-1 i_sigma f:F→B.

assertion.quantifiers: For these embeddings there exists an invertible b implementing their specified field identification on every x.
assertion.parameter_range: Quadratic subfields of the characteristic-zero quaternion algebra B/Q.
assertion.uniformity: Existence for each pair only; no uniform degree or coherent choices in sigma.
assertion.constants: No quantitative bound is supplied.
assertion.normalizations: j=b^-1 i b and g=f b^-1; quasi-homomorphisms are rationalized Hom. Positive integer denominator clearing is a separate elementary step.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An unspecified conjugacy of unlabelled subfields is insufficient. b need not be integral. The official erratum corrects unit-group notation after separable extension; no inseparable case or deleted optional splitting-field parenthesis is used.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain f and full End=B first; conjugate the specified embeddings, then clear denominators. Same-L descent, compatibility, cocycles, Q-descent and quantitative bounds are separate.

assertion.statement: The actual D210 quaternionic surface has potentially good reduction everywhere, and E=L(A[11]) is Galois over Q with [E:Q]<2^66; A has good reduction over E at every residue characteristic different from11.
assertion.objects: The actual A/L with rational quaternion division action and all geometric Hom over the normal fiber field L, its full11-torsion field E and the semistable special-fiber torus.
assertion.hypotheses: The D210 normalizer and same-L Hom construction are supplied. The published semistable reduction and full-torsion criteria, Neron extension property and torus structure are retained. The normalizer maps can be scaled prime to11 using the split maximal order at11.
assertion.quantifiers: Every place of A, and every conjugate of the full torsion field E; the good-reduction conclusion over E is for residue characteristics other than11.
assertion.parameter_range: Dimension two, division quaternion algebra B of discriminant210, degree[L:Q]≤576 and auxiliary prime11.
assertion.uniformity: The same Galois field E suffices simultaneously at2,3,5,7; no unbounded new extension is used for the later degree estimate.
assertion.normalizations: A positive torus rank t≤2 would give an injective unital B→M_t(Q), impossible for t=1 by dimension and for t=2 by division versus split algebra. Prime-to11 isogenies identify conjugate11-torsion kernels over L.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The full-torsion reduction criterion is not applied at residue characteristic11. Potential good reduction alone does not imply the explicit field E is Galois; that uses normalizer maps prime to11.
assertion.limit_order: Pass temporarily to semistable reduction and exclude torus rank; construct prime-to11 conjugate isogenies over L; prove E is Galois and bound its degree; apply the full11-torsion criterion and torus argument.

assertion.statement: For an abelian variety over a characteristic-zero field, rational matrix units give abelian image factors over that same field, mutually isogenous via off-diagonal units; complementary images sum by an isogeny.
assertion.objects: The original A/L with its L-defined M2(k) action, diagonal idempotents e11,e22 and a common positive integer denominator m.
assertion.hypotheses: The idempotents and matrix units belong to End_L^0(A); the image construction uses properness, geometric connectedness, and smoothness of finite-type group schemes in characteristic zero (the retained Cartier input).
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational matrix-unit system on this same abelian variety and every common denominator clearing it.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; here dim A=2 and the two matrix-unit factors have equal positive dimension.
assertion.uniformity: All images and maps are defined over L; no further field extension is introduced.
assertion.constants: Choose any positive integer m clearing the matrix-unit denominators; no uniform isogeny-degree bound is asserted by this algebraic construction.
assertion.normalizations: X_i=image(m e_ii); addition p and tuple q satisfy pq=[m] and qp=[m]. Off-diagonal units provide rational isomorphisms between X_i, and End^0(X_i)=e_ii End^0(A)e_ii.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Images do not depend on the chosen denominator. This is not a polarization-preserving isogeny assertion and does not give a good-reduction field bound or a quantitative isogeny estimate.
assertion.limit_order: First obtain L-defined full endomorphisms; then clear denominators, construct the images, and use the matrix-unit identities. Dimension two gives elliptic factors; the corner k gives CM.

assertion.statement: The two actual extra Kummer classes on E_n and E_(n theta), after restricted RC and forward analytic-rank-one imply Sha[2]=0, produce exactly eleven rational witnesses for the original pole template with the same B and m.
assertion.objects: Points(x1,y1),(x2,y2), x_i=A q_i^2, H=theta c^2, e=n/q1^2,z=c q2/q1,r1=y1/q1^3,r2=c^3 y2/(q1^3 z),w=(eHz)^(-1), and the six already chosen bits of m.
assertion.hypotheses: Both n,n theta are positive squarefree congruent11 mod12, with full2-Selmer dimension3, full2-infinity Selmer corank1 and extra class(beta,1) outside all rational2-torsion images. Retain restricted RC, rational modularity and the forward rank-one theorem.
assertion.quantifiers: For the original fixed B,m,A,H and the simultaneous pair n,n theta, choose rational representatives of their actual Kummer classes only after proving Sha[2]=0.
assertion.parameter_range: All q_i,c,e,z are nonzero rational numbers; theta=1 is allowed.
assertion.uniformity: Works for every B in the PC domain supplied by the simultaneous construction; no extra independent multiplier choice.
assertion.constants: Exactly the original six bits and five rational witnesses; no new template variables.
assertion.normalizations: Second point is(Az^2,z r2) on E_(eH). Dividing its cubic equation by z^2 yields r2^2=A(Az^2-eH)(Az^2+3eH), retaining leading factor A.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Extra class excludes infinity and all root points, so ordinates/abscissas and all denominators are nonzero. If theta=1 reuse one point and take q2=q1. Finite Sha is concluded from forward rank only, never assumed for RC.
assertion.limit_order: Exact Selmer dimension then full corank, then two restricted RC applications, then forward rank and Sha[2]=0, then actual points and final rational scaling.

assertion.statement: For the actual elliptic curve E/Q, the Cassels–Tate pairing induces a nondegenerate alternating pairing on the quotient of Sha(E) by its maximal divisible subgroup, hence on its finite2-primary quotient F in the supplied decomposition.
assertion.objects: The canonical principal polarization on E, Sha(E), its maximal divisible subgroup, and F=Sha(E)[2∞]/Sha(E)[2∞]_div.
assertion.hypotheses: E is an elliptic curve over Q. The supplied finite-Selmer/cofinite-generation input gives Sha(E)[2∞]=(Q2/Z2)^t⊕F with F finite. No finiteness of the full Sha group is assumed.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve E/Q; the finite-quotient application holds for its actual2-primary decomposition.
assertion.parameter_range: Canonical genus-one principal polarization;2-primary quotient by maximal divisibility, not the unrestricted pairing on2-torsion.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative bound or uniform finiteness statement.
assertion.constants: The quotient has paired finite primary cyclic factors; in particular dim_F2 F[2] is even.
assertion.normalizations: Cor4 gives c via Pic^(g−1); at g=1 the trivial degree-zero class makes c=0. Cor7 gives alternation. Nondegeneracy is after maximal-divisible quotient. Different primary torsion components are orthogonal.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not equate infinitely divisible elements with the maximal divisible subgroup in an arbitrary group. Current decomposition proves maximality directly. Do not infer nondegeneracy of the restriction to F[2], or finiteSha, or Mordell–Weil rank1 before RC.
assertion.limit_order: First use the separately supplied decomposition and identify its maximal divisible subgroup. Then restrict the quotient pairing to the finite2-primary part and apply the paired-factor argument; only afterward combine with Kummer dimensions.

assertion.quantifiers: For every such B choose m first, then beta,theta; construct one compatible auxiliary-prime assignment for both supports before selecting the actual primes.
assertion.parameter_range: beta>1,theta>=1 are coprime positive squarefree and prime to6; all auxiliary primes are distinct and avoid6 beta theta.
assertion.uniformity: The block determinant argument works for arbitrary d=omega(beta)>=1 and every finite theta support; no finite matrix test substitutes for it.
assertion.constants: The original2730 multiplier catalogue and old-prime valuation4 remain fixed; exactly d-1 I slots plus one q0 slot are used.

assertion.exceptional_cases: d=1 has empty I block; theta=1 permits identical two parameters. Necessary dyadic conditions give only an upper bound; the particular(beta,1) is separately checked locally at every place and independent of rational2-torsion.
assertion.limit_order: Reconcile all Legendre and local conditions before CRT/Dirichlet. Establish exact finite Selmer dimension before full-corank deduction or either use of RC; no rational point or finite Sha inferred here.

assertion.statement: For the retained fixed-field common family, there are Delta,Q in O[G] with u_x=2^(-a) eta_x Q_x/Delta_x^3 wherever Delta_x!=0. With f=2^a Delta^4 and d=eta Delta Q, f_x u_x=d_x holds at every character, f0 lies in Lambda, v2 f0(0)<=c_det and the signwise negative Laurent cutoff is L_T(M)=16(d_K+5)M.
assertion.objects: The actual cycle z, closed integral functional mu=2^a lambda_z, corrected coordinate u, retained determinant unit kappa, original group ring O[G], and grouped central Smith disk blocks A_i with Delta=product det A_i.
assertion.hypotheses: The preceding fixed-field budget gives the retained finite free family and m<=d_K+5, central rank-one cohomology and integral new-local cancellation. The actual paired functional and correction eta are supplied by their separate constructions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every sign character, including those where Delta_x=0, and every positive precision M for the Laurent bound.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed K and common family; O is the 2-adic completion of Lambda_(2), Lambda=Z2[[t]].
assertion.uniformity: The constants d_K,t_K,h_K are fixed after K and before the graph or binary dimension; a and c_E precede that choice.
assertion.constants: c_det=a+4(h_K+2c_E+2t_K); L_T(M)=16(d_K+5)M; denominator exponent3 and clearing power4 are fixed.
assertion.normalizations: Use the same actual z, functional, determinant basis and eta. Each grouped disk block is canceled once, and the inverse-determinant sign yields P=epsilon product_even delta_i^2.
assertion.exceptional_cases: When Delta_x=0 both f_x and d_x vanish, so no fraction with zero denominator is specialized. Acyclic constituents have the already defined zero coordinate. Only signwise Laurent support is bounded; no group-basis pole bound or bound for d is asserted.
assertion.limit_order: Cancel new local blocks retaining kappa; choose the constant central Smith bases; form original A_i determinants; cancel each grouped block once; then form Delta,Q,f,d in the original group ring before sign evaluation.

assertion.statement: At an actual derivative prime with nonzero finite localization of the rank-one generic actual class, switching from finite to singular condition produces a generic kernel spanned by its actual derivative and preserves the valuation of the class-functional determinant coordinate.
assertion.objects: The actual split derivative local model D0 plus(F plus S)[−1] plus D2[−2], its retained pairing, and the strict/relaxed/finite/singular Selmer cone complexes.
assertion.hypotheses: The old actual class spans generic H1 and localizes to nonzero v; its actual derivative has finite coordinate0 and singular coordinateJv. Retained integral local pairings/isotropy homotopies and exact global duality/localization identities are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: At each new inert derivative prime in the finite sequence, over the stated fraction or test field.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite and singular planes of rank2; localization v may be divisible in the integral lattice.
assertion.uniformity: The comparison preserves valuation at every allowed switch, without requiring a uniform divisibility bound on v.
assertion.constants: The common strict determinant factor, including all strict torsion, is retained on both sides; exterior-volume changes are units.
assertion.normalizations: Every condition retains D0; relaxed means D0 plus(F plus S)[−1], not the full local complex. Cross pairing is epsilon times <x,Jy>. Fractional complements are chosen to have unit exterior volume.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not require the complement of a divisible v to be integral. Exact annihilator follows from duality/localization, not isotropy alone. The derivative must be the actual class, not a substituted primitive vector.
assertion.limit_order: Retain the integral local model and triangles; pass to the specified test field; identify strict H1 and the relaxed annihilator; use the actual derivative; compare determinant lines with their common strict factor.

components.connecting_argument: For an empty unit choose one actual stage with precision above delta_o: the D=1 coefficient is visible, so RC follows immediately. Otherwise fix the permitted unit k before b; its nonzero central value gives twist corank zero by the separate forward theorem. A fresh ramified prime of quadratic K is unramified in each old label normal closure and in Q(E[8]); hence K cannot lie in those fields and its intersection with each is Q. Old labels have lifts split in K. Stabilize the actual common alphabet on the same ultrafilter, retaining all relations and only separate projection surjectivity. Finally the restriction/corestriction sum-and-difference maps have kernels/cokernels killed by a fixed2-power; after tensoring compact Selmer modules with Q2 they give the plus/minus direct sum and add coranks. No integral direct sum or finite-Sha inference is made.

Combine these with the reduced class representing its type by CRT; the moduli are coprime after fixed support is separated. Dirichlet gives infinitely many primes in the resulting reduced class, so avoid all old and finitely excluded primes. Repeat for each new vertex and use reciprocity for reverse bits. The same construction realizes a permitted product-template type with all its external incidences. The separate graph-dependence theorem identifies the symbol values.

assertion.statement: The all-graph universal correction is independent of the arithmetic Frobenius lift and graph orientation, and its local two-place determinant has residual t-order exactly four at augmentation.
assertion.objects: The graph-wide actual finite moving characters, local scalar z_q, inertia generator g_q, e_q, l_q and correction1+(1+g_q)v_q in O[G].
assertion.hypotheses: The full graph prescription and compatible Kummer/ring-class realization are supplied; the universal group ring is two-torsion-free and e_q is a unit after inner limit/localization.
assertion.quantifiers: Every graph prime q, including those unused by a constituent and those seen at augmentation, in each fixed finite binary family.
assertion.parameter_range: Good odd q and O[G] after the retained inner limit; finite character stages are handled before these inverses.
assertion.uniformity: Enlarging Q changes the finite realization field but not the fixed trace bound c_E.
assertion.constants: Modulo(2,I_G), e_q=t²/(1+t), l_q=t⁴/(1+t)²; augmentation determinant q⁴l_q has order four.
assertion.normalizations: Replacing Frobenius lift sends z_q to g_q z_q; quotient agreement gives(1+g_q)(vprime_q-v_q)=0 by two-torsion-freeness. Reversing orientation sends z_q to its inverse and preserves e_q,l_q.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An active ramified constituent is not assigned an unramified Frobenius eigenvalue. The finite characters need not be restrictions of one infinite Galois character.
assertion.limit_order: Prescribe all Q before moving-prime selection; realize finite characters and retain diagram limits; invert e_q only after localization; prove lift/orientation invariance before forming the finite product.

assertion.statement: The actual primitive class-functional coordinate is regular at every height-one prime of Lambda other than(2), including(t) and(t+2), hence belongs to Lambda[1/2]. This regularity also holds at the unknown full-corank-one base.
assertion.objects: The actual primitive scalar Selmer complex, its actual class and own paired functional, and the integral derivative-switch complexes over each height-one DVR.
assertion.hypotheses: The starting generic kernel has rank one unless the actual class is zero; evaluation injection, characteristic-zero detection, exact local duality and actual-class determinant switch identities are supplied. Primitive integrality holds for the old local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every height-one prime different from(2), and each finite derivative list produced by the argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Known simple-zero ring instances and the unknown full-corank-one base, with the latter used only for regularity.
assertion.uniformity: No uniform numerical valuation bound at the unknown base is asserted. Finite switch termination is pointwise for the height-one test.
assertion.constants: All switch determinant factors are units; no new numerical constant or inverse localization value is introduced.
assertion.normalizations: At quadratic specialization the two signs are defined by actual conjugation, not a ring substitution. Finite and singular planes carry opposite J actions and exact symmetric hyperbolic cross pairing. Retain D0, strict torsion factors and the actual class-functional product.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At(t) and(t+2) use sign splitting and one-or-two-step descent, not nonquadratic irreducibility. Isotropy alone does not prove U=U-perp. Primitive vectors select primes but never replace the actual class. No inverse at an unused relaxed prime.
assertion.limit_order: Localize at a height-one prime; choose a primitive generic-kernel vector for detection; use actual derivative switches until dimension one; show the actual class and own functional integral there; transport unit-valued determinant comparisons back; intersect all height-one localizations.

components.connecting_argument: At size r>=2 a nonzero derivative in one internal bit would equal a unit contracted symbol on r-1 positive vertices, contradicting minimality. At r=1 there is no such bit. Repeated derivatives along the contraction forest give its unit terminal value, proving the original multilinear polynomial nonzero. Keep r-1 type anchors and merge the nonempty remainder: equality of total type forces the final seed type. Minimum-seed independence removes internal-bit choices. Addresses use only nonzero linear activations; formal bit variables do not alter the already fixed initial prime realization.

assertion.statement: There is one integral universal correction eta in O[G] such that the same corrected relaxed coordinate tilde_u=eta*u_rel satisfies tilde_u_x=epsilon_x*u_prim,x at every character, with epsilon_x a Lambda unit. Central valuations and zeros transfer whenever the primitive coordinate is regular.
assertion.objects: Actual primitive-to-relaxed map i and paired strict map j, actual retained classes and their own closed functionals, unused-prime factors e_q=a_q-z-z^(-1), two-place quotient factor l_q, and finite binary groupG.
assertion.hypotheses: The retained norm identity and boundary, cup-pairing naturality and original integral determinant bases are supplied. Every graph prime, including unused ones, has the prescribed scalar exponent. Rational E[2] makes a_q even at good oddq.
assertion.quantifiers: Each unused good split prime and every character of the same finite binary family, with one eta before character evaluation.
assertion.parameter_range: Lambda=Z2[[t]], O its completed localization at(2); good oddq and common graph-wide moving character.
assertion.uniformity: The correction is constructed in the original O[G] for the whole family, without character-by-character interpolation or group-order denominators.
assertion.constants: l_q*u_rel=e_q^2*epsilon_q*u_prim; q^2*l_q=e_q^2+(q-1)(q-1-(z+z^(-1))*e_q); v_q=(l_q/e_q^2-1)/2.
assertion.normalizations: Both the actual class and its own paired functional contribute onee_q. Comparison signs and unit disks give Lambda units, not merelyO units. eta is the product of1+v_q(1+g_q).
assertion.exceptional_cases: eta_x can have a pole at t=0; only its product withu_rel,x is specialized. No integral self-duality of the primitive condition or interpolation ofepsilon_x is assumed.
assertion.limit_order: Use the actual norm boundary and pairing naturality; compare quotient determinants in retained bases; prove e_q is anO[G]unit via reduction t^2/(1+t); construct integralv_q and oneeta; then evaluate characters and transfer regular central data.

assertion.statement: For the retained global, primitive and derivative Selmer models, finite detecting evaluations give an H1 injection preserved by coefficient extension; their bounded outer quotient is a characteristic-zero DVR with uniformizer2, carrying the retained duality maps and approximate cycles as actual crossed homomorphisms.
assertion.objects: Actual retained cochain maps, product Galois groups, bounded finite detecting lists, primitive/derivative local conditions and O_infinity formed from valuation-bounded ring instances.
assertion.hypotheses: Fixed bounded minimal-model ranks, omega(k_j)≤A and a fixed number of derivative labels; retained evaluations and compatibility homotopies. Direct Selmer evaluation requires residual H0 isomorphism and H1 injection for the local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every indicated coefficient extension and each sequence of the bounded ring instances; evaluation at arbitrary sequences of group elements.
assertion.parameter_range: Primitive and derivative models with the stated local conditions. Orthogonal zero/full models only after an actual contraction at the chosen test ring.
assertion.uniformity: Detecting lists have bounded length at most dimV+dimW, selected and padded before the common limit. No support-uniform rank beyond the stipulated bound.
assertion.constants: Uniformizer2; no quantitative rank bound is added beyond the retained (5.1) bound.
assertion.normalizations: O_infinity is the ultraproduct quotient by sequences whose 2-adic valuation tends to infinity. Cochain evaluation uses the same ultrafilter, full compatibility homotopies and integral minimal-model inverses.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No continuity claim on one original Galois group and no completeness claim for the outer DVR. Zero local conditions may contribute evaluation-invisible H1, so direct injection is not asserted there. Approximate cycles are not silently replaced by exact finite-stage cycles.
assertion.limit_order: Choose finite detecting lists and cone cancellations before the common inner limit; form the bounded outer quotient; pass actual matrices and homotopies; only then regard differential-tending-to-zero sequences as crossed homomorphisms.

use.reason: Use Gamma=Gamma0(N) and the normalized simultaneous eigenfunction; the level group lies in the required range. The quotient is over Q and has dimension [Q:Q]=1. The unital Q-coefficient action is integer multiplication on integral scalars. Shimura's eigenrelation includes all its T_n. This card consumes its good-prime relation and its almost-all Euler comparison. Pulling back differentials along z to qz and (z+j)/q gives exactly q f(qz)+q^-1 sum_j f((z+j)/q). Moduli cyclic quotients and their duals exchange the two projections for q coprime to N. Use the same J0(N) and q_f on the degree-zero divisor classes, not a polarisation-dual map or a tangent-space substitute. No degree or averaging factor is inserted. A rationalized morphism equality descends to integral Hom by torsion-freeness. The good correspondence has q+1 branches at infinity, all fixing it. The rational cusp gives the Pic0 map and no extra constant. The Gamma0(N) branch makes the alternative Fricke condition unnecessary. No bad Euler, Atkin–Lehner, integral lattice or model extension conclusion is claimed. Postcompose with alpha and apply to [x]-[infinity]. The unaveraged CM and reduced neighbor relations consume this operator with their separate CM and reduction inputs.

components.connecting_argument: Partitionability gives a nonzero stationary terminal polynomial. Build arbitrarily large cubes based at the unchanged d with unit symbols at all other addresses. Their scalar valuations have one fixed bound after the same denominator clearing. Fix precision above that bound and use a cube dimension larger than the sum of the bounded bit degrees. The Boolean comparison gives a nonzero address congruent to the base at that precision. A zero or larger-valuation base would force the same at this address, contradicting its unit bound. Use the central corank-zero comparison to obtain the stated normalized L-value bound. The required dimension may depend on d; C1 does not. Empty units use the direct coefficient bound instead.

Finite-stage Chebotarev realizes it with exact inner-limit basis-cochain matrix equality before minimal-model denominators.
assertion.objects: The exact kernel on the full Tate module, all retained ring-class and quadratic fields; two evaluated cohomology classes; their finite localizations and original cochain basis matrices.
assertion.hypotheses: The fixed nontrivial scalar element survives the characteristic-zero test; actual evaluation is injective. The fixed matrix-span witness gives absolutely irreducible rank-two summands; moving scalar character is nonquadratic and conjugation exchanges summands. Finite quotient cochain data and finite Chebotarev are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: For each such pair of independent classes and the specified finite-stage data, there is an actual kernel element and a compatible finite-stage prime/place.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero inner or outer fraction-field tests with nonquadratic moving character. Residual characteristic2 assertions are expressly weaker.
assertion.uniformity: The same inner ultrafilter gives exact matrix equality for each retained outer instance before its possibly varying denominators.
assertion.constants: No uniform denominator bound is assumed; only the existing bounded cohomology/detecting-list inputs are used.
assertion.normalizations: Kernel restriction uses the central scalar modulo the kernel, not an element inside it. Equality L_j=E_(sigma_j squared) is between original Lambda matrices before composition with I_j.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No residual irreducibility or residual rank-two localization is asserted. Quadratic height-one specializations require their separate proof. assertion.limit_order: Obtain the kernel element on the characteristic-zero test; place all original cochain/Tate/field data in one compatible finite compositum; choose prime and place; pass to exact inner matrix identity; only then apply minimal-model maps.

historical_source_navigation.title: Kato rational Euler-system divisibility
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: T2E and quadratic twists with cyclotomic inverse deck action; full coefficient ring A=Z2[[t]][1/2].
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Euler norm relation, nonzero generic class in both real components, each real eigenspace rank1, purity, rational irreducibility, cyclotomic-kernel element with one-dimensional fixed space. Open image supplies latter two.

historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Apply13.4(2) at each height-one prime not containing2; separate local cone comparison and fixed F_E promote H2_0 to the full target. Part(3), whose residual hypotheses fail, is excluded.

historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite normal closures of: the Hilbert class field; the moving-character radical/cyclotomic/Tate compositum; the fixed witness division torsor; finite quotients for the original basis cochains; and joint finite reductions of weight-two constituent representations. Each prescribed element is the restriction of an actual Galois element, and each non-class-function use selects a place realizing that representative.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: The moving radical multipliers respect every Kummer relation; Tate adjustment lies in the actual radical-fixing kernel. The witness detector uses one h*tau before precision varies. Finite cochains factor through finite quotients, made normal over Q before applying density. Joint representation reductions and actual elements make trace prescriptions compatible. Each extension is finite Galois and the conjugacy class nonempty; exclusions are finite.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p). A rational prime supplies a conjugacy class; the chosen place fixes its representative and transported coordinates. Cochain equality is established at increasing finite precision before multiplying by localized minimal-model inclusions. No infinite-level density assertion or independent constituent prescriptions.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: The explicit composita, maps and nonempty classes for every registered use are given in batch 8. Existing Hilbert-class, open-image, Kummer, kernel-detection and coefficient/local-representation inputs are retained as dependencies. In particular this does not close A032, A064, A068, A070 or A080.

historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Part I Theorem 12.1(a), p. 55; Theorem 10.15, p. 49; Proposition 10.20, p. 50; Lemma 14.5, p. 63; Part IV Theorem 3.5, pp. 141-142 and Lemma 3.9, p. 143.
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: W0=Res_K/Q A, geometric End lattice rank≤16F0²; Galois kernel E; L=EK.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consumes the earlier finite-etale cover and good reduction construction and the restriction-of-scalars abelian variety W0.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Unramified versus good reduction: prime-to-residue coefficient prime; action on ordered conjugacy Hom comes via End(W0), not arbitrary labels.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Milne I.10.15 bounds integral endomorphism rank; a finite basis descends over a finite extension. A finite-order integral action congruent to identity mod 3 has eigenvalues 1 by I.14.5 and is semisimple in characteristic zero, so reduction modulo 3 is faithful. NOS and unramified induction show inertia acts trivially on Tate and hence End away from T. Passing to EK fixes the factor labels and all ordered Hom groups.

historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Conductor1 and ramified determinant rule out special/supercuspidal cases; obtain one unramified and one ramified line. Integral trace identity follows from diagonal matrices without dividing by2 or using integral eigenspace projectors.

historical_source_navigation.conventions: Additive character sign, Fourier kernel, determinant/Hilbert symbol and inverse Weil index must be matched together. Compare with rank1 Q0 to remove scalar multiplier.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Apply explicit unipotent, diagonal and Fourier operators. Manuscript derives square-invariance of the local index and finite-character quotient instead of choosing incompatible square roots.

historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite normal closures of: the Hilbert class field; the moving-character radical/cyclotomic/Tate compositum; the fixed witness division torsor; finite quotients for the original basis cochains; and joint finite reductions of weight-two constituent representations. Each prescribed element is the restriction of an actual Galois element, and each non-class-function use selects a place realizing that representative.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: The moving radical multipliers respect every Kummer relation; Tate adjustment lies in the actual radical-fixing kernel. The witness detector uses one h*tau before precision varies. Finite cochains factor through finite quotients, made normal over Q before applying density. Joint representation reductions and actual elements make trace prescriptions compatible. Each extension is finite Galois and the conjugacy class nonempty; exclusions are finite.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p). A rational prime supplies a conjugacy class; the chosen place fixes its representative and transported coordinates. Cochain equality is established at increasing finite precision before multiplying by localized minimal-model inclusions. No infinite-level density assertion or independent constituent prescriptions.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: The explicit composita, maps and nonempty classes for every registered use are given in batch 8. historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite normal closures of: the Hilbert class field; the moving-character radical/cyclotomic/Tate compositum; the fixed witness division torsor; finite quotients for the original basis cochains; and joint finite reductions of weight-two constituent representations. historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: The moving radical multipliers respect every Kummer relation; Tate adjustment lies in the actual radical-fixing kernel. The witness detector uses one h*tau before precision varies. Finite cochains factor through finite quotients, made normal over Q before applying density. Joint representation reductions and actual elements make trace prescriptions compatible. Each extension is finite Galois and the conjugacy class nonempty; exclusions are finite.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p). A rational prime supplies a conjugacy class; the chosen place fixes its representative and transported coordinates. Cochain equality is established at increasing finite precision before multiplying by localized minimal-model inclusions. No infinite-level density assertion or independent constituent prescriptions.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: The explicit composita, maps and nonempty classes for every registered use are given in batch 8. Existing Hilbert-class, open-image, Kummer, kernel-detection and coefficient/local-representation inputs are retained as dependencies. In particular this does not close A032, A064, A068, A070 or A080.

historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Carayol sections 0.3-0.7, Theorem A pp.409-411; Casselman Theorem 1 pp.302-306, corollary p.306, Theorem 4 p.313
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Weight-two constituents obtained by multiplying weight3/2 form by theta; odd p with new level exponent1 and primitive ramified quadratic character.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: F=Q has odd degree, so no extra finite discrete-series place. All cusp eigenconstituents, old multiplicities and Eisenstein terms handled. Coefficient place lies over2; local residue p is odd.

historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Conductor1 and ramified determinant rule out special/supercuspidal cases; obtain one unramified and one ramified line. Integral trace identity follows from diagonal matrices without dividing by2 or using integral eigenspace projectors.

historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Ring-class quotient by K^* and completed order units; arithmetic local/global Artin maps; residue-ratio inclusion delta at a split moving prime; norm pullback of quadratic characters; derivative-prime relative kernels and conjugation action.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Use invertible order ideals, K imaginary with units +/-1, conductors outside 2ND_K and containing the actual finite-character supports. historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p), positive prime ideal classes. The local-idelic delta is the negative of the ray principal-residue map, yielding the negative weighted Kummer prescription. Coefficient rings are fixed under Galois pullback.

historical_source_navigation.title: Compactness, ultrafilter and finite intersection
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Stacks Tags 086J and 08ZY, exact HTML snapshots of 2026-11-05; Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2 p.155, VIII Corollary 7.3 p.258; direct common-alphabet and finite-stage arguments in closure-batch-006 and closure-batch-007
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consume the actual quadratic coefficient factorization, fresh ramification of K, fixed nonempty seeds and detector stages with ell_0=-1 mod 2^M. Fresh ramification proves disjointness; the determinant congruence makes finite prime exclusions cofinite. Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

historical_source_navigation.title: Compactness, ultrafilter and finite intersection
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Stacks Tags 086J and 08ZY, exact HTML snapshots of 2026-11-05; Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2 p.155, VIII Corollary 7.3 p.258; direct common-alphabet and finite-stage arguments in closure-batch-006 and closure-batch-007
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consume the actual quadratic coefficient factorization, fresh ramification of K, fixed nonempty seeds and detector stages with ell_0=-1 mod 2^M. Fresh ramification proves disjointness; the determinant congruence makes finite prime exclusions cofinite. Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Stacks Tags 086J and 08ZY, exact HTML snapshots of 2026-11-05; Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2 p.155, VIII Corollary 7.3 p.258; direct common-alphabet and finite-stage arguments in closure-batch-006 and closure-batch-007
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consume the actual quadratic coefficient factorization, fresh ramification of K, fixed nonempty seeds and detector stages with ell_0=-1 mod 2^M. Fresh ramification proves disjointness; the determinant congruence makes finite prime exclusions cofinite. Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

assertion.statement: For Q_kappa in five variables obtain the uniform nonprimitive count needed before the displayed Mobius inversion.
assertion.objects: The five-variable nondegenerate isotropic Q_kappa, kappa!=0, nonnegative smooth weight away from zero, and arbitrary nonempty sets of nonzero good-modulus quadric residues.
assertion.hypotheses: n=5 is permitted (n≥5, not n>5). Qκ has κ≠0, rank5 and rational isotropic point (1,0,1,0,0). Modulus squarefree, coprime to2κ, hence to2ΔQ; each residue subset is in nonzero zeros. Smooth compact support away from origin, so gradient bounded away from0. Error B^(n/2+ε)m^(n/2+ε) uniform in modulus/subsets; derivatives may depend on fixedτ. The weight is nonnegative; empty allowed sets are handled by the zero count.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: n=5 is permitted (n≥5, not n>5). Qκ has κ≠0, rank5 and rational isotropic point (1,0,1,0,0). Modulus squarefree, coprime to2κ, hence to2ΔQ; each residue subset is in nonzero zeros. Smooth compact support away from origin, so gradient bounded away from0. Error B^(n/2+ε)m^(n/2+ε) uniform in modulus/subsets; derivatives may depend on fixedτ. The weight is nonnegative; empty allowed sets are handled by the zero count.
assertion.uniformity: Rescale by h in Möbius sum. For (h,m)=1, h^-1Ω has same size; otherwise no contribution. Sum errors absolutely and calculate local densities.
assertion.constants: For an isotropic nondegenerate integral quadratic form F in n>=5 variables and a nonnegative smooth compactly supported weight away from the gradient-zero locus, the weighted count of all integral zeros satisfying nonempty admissible sets of local zeros that are nonzero modulo each relevant prime has the product-density main term and error O_(epsilon,F,w)(B^(n/2+epsilon) M^(n/2+epsilon)), uniformly in M and allowed subsets when M is coprime to twice the discriminant.
assertion.normalizations: BL counts all integral zeros; appendix imposes global primitivity by Möbius inversion. Hessian/determinant discriminant conventions differ only by powers of2 here. Primitive local density is1−p^-4; conditioning denominator p^4−1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Empty local sets contribute zero; n=5 is allowed. Primitive normalization is obtained by the separate Mobius sum.
assertion.limit_order: Fix kappa, the smooth nonnegative weight and tau before varying B and the admissible squarefree modulus.

assertion.uniformity: Each i has a block of active variables absent from each competing form. Apply normal-form GN, then divide by the added box cardinality.
assertion.constants: A finite-complexity system of nonzero pairwise nonproportional affine-linear forms can be extended to the stated normal form by adjoining variables and using the given invertible integer change of variables.

assertion.statement: Bound the first and second shifted-majorant moments in the boundary argument and obtain weighted L2 control.
assertion.objects: In a fixed enlarged ambient interval without wrap, isolate at most one constant-shift factor nu0. Set F(x)=E_m product_i nu_i(x+P_i(m)). Apply to nu0*F, nu0*F^2, nu0.
assertion.hypotheses: In F^2 use independent m and mprime; every pairwise difference of the nonconstant shifts, including across the two copies, is nonconstant. All degrees and counts are fixed, coefficients fall within A^C, and the parameter box lengths exceed the required logarithmic lower bound. The sieve exponent is chosen small enough for this enlarged moment family.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: In F^2 use independent m and mprime; every pairwise difference of the nonconstant shifts, including across the two copies, is nonconstant. All degrees and counts are fixed, coefficients fall within A^C, and the parameter box lengths exceed the required logarithmic lower bound. The sieve exponent is chosen small enough for this enlarged moment family.
assertion.uniformity: The three moments give E nu0*(F-1)^2=o(1). Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz reduces any interval-strip mass to E1_I*nu0; V6-GA-GT-INTERVAL-MEAN supplies that mean.
assertion.constants: The polynomial-forms estimate for the normalized divisor-sum majorant gives the stated asymptotic for a fixed family whose pairwise shift differences are nonconstant, over the full cyclic base variable and permitted parameter boxes, with cutoff-then-size errors.
assertion.normalizations: The source theorem averages x over the whole cyclic group; no x-subinterval conclusion is quoted. Errors retain cutoff-then-size order, o_(v to infinity)(1)+o_v(1).
assertion.exceptional_cases: The global cyclic moment estimate does not by itself imply interval mean control; the latter is separately imported.
assertion.limit_order: Freeze polynomial family, complexity and cutoff before size; apply the second-moment estimate to independent copies.

assertion.statement: Pass to the conjugated rational subgroup quotient on each periodic class and recenter the translated test function there.
assertion.objects: H_j=gamma_j^(-1)*G-prime*gamma_j; Lambda_j=H_j intersect Gamma; h_j=gamma_j^(-1)*g-prime*gamma_j. F_jk(x Lambda_j)=F(a_jk*gamma_j*x Gamma).
assertion.hypotheses: Reduced gamma_j has rational coordinates of height M^O(1); a_jk=epsilon(n_jk) has bounded M-power coordinates. The output subgroup basis and lattice satisfy the published claim.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Reduced gamma_j has rational coordinates of height M^O(1); a_jk=epsilon(n_jk) has bounded M-power coordinates. The output subgroup basis and lattice satisfy the published claim.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain basis rationality M^C2, total M^(-aB+C2)-equidistribution and Lip norm M^C2. Account for commensurable lattices and finite-index losses; conjugation is not an isometry of the original quotients. Subtract each new quotient Haar mean, including the dimension-zero case. The claim is used for a general weight through separate mean/minor-arc hypotheses, not by extending the Möbius theorem.
assertion.constants: The published quantitative conjugation claim transfers a rational subgroup orbit to the conjugated quotient with the actual intersection lattice, controlling rationality, equidistribution and Lipschitz losses by fixed powers of the height bound.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The quotient comparison is not an isometry; finite-index and Lipschitz losses and the zero-dimensional case remain explicit.
assertion.limit_order: Fix B and the resulting M, then permit fixed powers of M in the new basis, metric and equidistribution losses.

assertion.objects: Initial polynomial g on G/Gamma, M0=log(2N)^max(1,C_init), external exponent A renamed B; g=epsilon*g-prime*gamma.
assertion.hypotheses: Initial basis is log(2N)^C_init-rational, hence M0-rational; fixed dimension m, degree d. Output M0<=M<=C*M0^E(B), rational subgroup G-prime and Gamma-prime=G-prime intersect Gamma.

assertion.uniformity: epsilon is (M,N)-smooth, g-prime totally M^(-B)-equidistributed, gamma rational with coset period q<=M. B is chosen using lower M>=log(2N) before E(B) is used for the later progression threshold; no circular comparison B>E(B).
assertion.constants: The quantitative polynomial-orbit factorization theorem gives g=epsilon g-prime gamma, where epsilon is (M,N)-smooth, g-prime is totally M^(-B)-equidistributed on a rational subgroup, and gamma has rational coset period at most M, for M between M0 and a fixed power of M0 depending on the chosen B.

assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not require a circular inequality B>E(B); the lower logarithmic bound supplies the needed decay.
assertion.limit_order: Choose the desired equidistribution exponent B from the lower bound M>=M_0 before using the resulting E(B).

available_assertion.statement: Reduction gives an equivalence between finite etale algebras over a henselian local ring and finite etale algebras over its residue field.
available_assertion.objects: A henselian local ring R and finite etale R-algebras.
available_assertion.hypotheses: R is henselian local.
available_assertion.quantifiers: For every instance satisfying the stated hypotheses.
available_assertion.parameter_range: All henselian local rings; no number-field or residue-characteristic restriction.
available_assertion.uniformity: Qualitative finite exclusions only; no bound or replacement of either controlled field or exceptional set.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical conductor, degree or height estimate is asserted.
available_assertion.normalizations: The equivalence is reduction modulo the maximal ideal.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion for a nonhenselian ring.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix the henselian local ring, then reduce its finite etale algebras.

needed_assertion.statement: Over the strict henselization the finite etale ell-power torsion splits into sections, giving a reduction bijection natural for transition maps and homomorphisms.
needed_assertion.objects: The finite etale torsion of the comparison surface over the strict henselian good local base.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Finite etaleness is separately supplied; the residue field of the strict henselization is separably closed.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: For every instance satisfying the stated hypotheses.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero number fields and good finite places; the coefficient prime differs from the residue characteristic.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Qualitative finite exclusions only; no bound or replacement of either controlled field or exceptional set.
needed_assertion.constants: No numerical conductor, degree or height estimate is asserted.
needed_assertion.normalizations: Reduction is natural; it respects [ell] and each spread m mu_sigma.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: No good reduction at the coefficient prime is inferred; bad or ramified places are excluded.
needed_assertion.limit_order: First obtain finite etale torsion; then split over the strict henselization and pass to inverse limits.

assertion.statement: The irreducible rational cubic H in the degree-obstruction argument is geometrically integral.
assertion.objects: The homogenized cubic H with forms X0,X1 and rational zeros of inputs0 and1.
assertion.hypotheses: H is irreducible over Q of degree3, has the two specified rational zeros, and every rational zero on X0=1 has integer input.
assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q; the actual cubic dimension>=2 branch where applicable.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
assertion.constants: No numerical constant is required.
assertion.normalizations: The input is X1/X0; the two zeros are normalized by X0=1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
assertion.limit_order: If geometrically reducible, irreducibility over Q makes the geometric factors one Galois orbit. Characteristic zero excludes repetition, so degree3 forces three conjugate linear factors. Every rational zero lies on all three; the rational line joining the two specified zeros remains in their intersection and realizes every rational input, contradiction.

assertion.statement: A nonconstant rational function on a nonempty rational affine open cannot take only integer values on its rational points.
assertion.objects: The composite of X1/X0 with the dominant rational parametrization of the actual quotient cubic.
assertion.hypotheses: The parametrization is dominant over Q; its domain meets the input chart in a nonempty open; X1/X0 is nonconstant.

assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q; the actual cubic dimension>=2 branch where applicable.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.

assertion.normalizations: Shrink to a rational affine principal open avoiding the denominator. No density of rational points on the cubic itself is assumed.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
assertion.limit_order: Dominance preserves nonconstancy in function fields. Choose a real ball in the affine principal open. Rational density and continuity put its whole image in the closed set Z; connectedness makes that image constant. The numerator minus this constant times the denominator vanishes on a real open ball, hence identically, contradiction.

use.reason: For the actual finite-rank group-ring coefficient, every finite quotient has finite H0. Thus its H0 images stabilize, giving Mittag-Leffler and zero lim1. The quotients by (2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1) and finite-group coefficient relations are cofinal with powers of the maximal ideal: the former quotient is finite local, hence has nilpotent maximal ideal; conversely its defining elements lie in any prescribed maximal-ideal power for sufficiently large a,n. Apply the source exact sequence to this cofinal system. The already proved norm compatibility supplies the compatible H1 elements; it is not supplied by this theorem. For K10 take R=Z_2[[Gamma]][G]=Z_2[[t]][G], where G is the fixed finite elementary abelian two-group, and take the free rank-two R-module T_2E tensor R with the actual continuous chi_0 psi kappa^(-1) action. R is a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m generated by2,t and g-1 for g in G; its residue field is F_2. The actual finite quotients use J_(a,n)=(2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1). The quotient R/J_(a,n) is finite and local: modulo2 it is the group algebra of the finite two-group Gamma_n times G, whose augmentation ideal is nilpotent. Hence some power of m is contained in J_(a,n). Conversely J_(a,n) is contained in any prescribed m^k for a,n sufficiently large: 2^a is in m^k for a>=k, while for 1<=i<k the coefficient binomial(2^n,i) has valuation at least n-v_2(i), and terms of degree i>=k are already in m^k. Thus these ideals and the m-adic powers define cofinal filtrations. Use a diagonal cofinal sequence in a,n. Each H0 of the finite quotient coefficient is a subgroup of a finite module, so its images stabilize and lim1 H0 vanishes. Apply Corollary4.1.3 to the complete finite-type admissible R-module through this cofinal identification. Norm compatibility of the already supplied classes produces their inverse-limit element; the argument proves no new norm relation.

use.reason: For an odd p, a character of the cyclic two-primary part of F_p^times can send its unique element of order two to minus one; the trivial character gives plus one. Pull back along reduction. At2 use the trivial or modulo-four character. Thus the prescribed sign is achieved without assuming it for an arbitrary character. The integral projectors preserve the selected-line convention; their support is supplied by the separate split-support application.
