source_hypotheses.required: Fixed s>=3, m=s-1, 1<=R<=m, a one-bounded f, an actual global unit A of multidegree (1,m), and a dense internal family of strongly represented unit nilcharacters chi_h of degree-rank (m,R), with positive derivative correlation witnessed by a uniformly bounded internal family of lower ordinary-degree tests.
source_hypotheses.constructed: The proof starts with that actual family and reselects models after every rank restart.
source_hypotheses.justification: Hereditary LP03 must hold after each dense restriction. Ordinary weak Definition6.19 objects alone do not supply the required all-limit identities.

constructed_objects.required: Produce core, bracket-linear and independent frequency data and actual real top annihilation.
constructed_objects.constructed: The lexicographically minimal B,L,C construction, nested restrictions and rational covers yield the frequency presentation.
constructed_objects.justification: Failed relations invoke the one-function F statement; D and a nonzero coset integral force the required real character vanishings.

index_domain_coverage.required: The same dense internal subfamily and all required weights must be covered.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: There are finitely many weights and finitely many standard refinements; all retained families use uniform standard geometry.
index_domain_coverage.justification: Finite density losses preserve a positive standard density. Fresh data are required for every restarted family.

transition_maps.required: Universal Hall coordinates must map integrally to the current model.
transition_maps.constructed: The algebraic Hall/quotient node supplies the weighted universal lattice; rational covers and basis changes update the map and character together.
transition_maps.justification: Powering generators and dividing frequencies use a common denominator. The associated character and representation map are not held unchanged under a basis change.

consumed_object_identity.required: The vanishings must apply to the actual character used in LP04.
consumed_object_identity.constructed: The nonzero Haar integral uses the actual shifted quadruple product and its actual lower-degree witness.
consumed_object_identity.justification: Rational periodic factors are killed by a standard multiplier rather than discarded; connected real powers then force real eta(w)=0, not merely an integer value.

coefficient_conventions.required: Keep horizontal Taylor classes, commutator errors and matrix coordinates distinct.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: Taylor maps are homomorphisms modulo the stated error groups; successor-rank terms vanish at the indicated top weight.
coefficient_conventions.justification: Core plus four B and any three L directions are independent at each weight on the retained tuples. Scalar frequency information alone is not the full LP04 tensor.

local_conditions.required: Localization must preserve a nonzero correlation.
local_conditions.constructed: Small coordinate circles, interval masks, a finite Lipschitz net and a common rational cover are chosen with errors below the existing bias.
local_conditions.justification: The interval-mask approximation is L1; unit padding is a fixed coordinate isometry, not equality of every varying test function.

exceptional_cases.required: Vanishing arguments must remain valid when some frequency families are empty.
exceptional_cases.constructed: Empty families give trivial conditions; finite refinements and rational-cover constructions still apply.
exceptional_cases.justification: There is no claim that arbitrary weak nilcharacters become strong, or that rank lowering at R>1 is ordinary degree lowering.

downstream_consumption.required: Supply the actual bad-word annihilations to LP04.
downstream_consumption.constructed: This node ends at the analytic frequency and real-vanishing output.
downstream_consumption.justification: The source also describes a later LP04/S12 join. That later invocation is excluded from this node and belongs to RANK/assembly, preventing a circular dependency through LP04.

source_hypotheses.required: Fixed weighted generators, m,R and an upward-closed monomial set.
source_hypotheses.constructed: The local proof uses the free Lie quotient with weight>m or weight=m and length>R removed.
source_hypotheses.justification: Tointon Definition5.4.3, Theorem5.4.5 and the end of Section5.4 supply the Hall normal forms; the local triangular BCH argument proves the particular lattice saturation.

constructed_objects.required: Construct a connected rational quotient with exact lattice intersections.
constructed_objects.constructed: The ideal generated by words with at least two petals or a discarded petal is exponentiated and divided out.
constructed_objects.justification: It is a normal subgroup and need not be central. Integral Hall coordinates give the lattice in this specific monomial quotient.

index_domain_coverage.required: All filtration indices and bad words at every weight must be included.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: Higher weights are included in every filtered group; the cutoff is not imposed only at the top.
index_domain_coverage.justification: Upward closure ensures bracket stability and the taut degree-rank filtration.

transition_maps.required: Provide the universal representation maps and petal rescalings.
transition_maps.constructed: The petal subgroup is abelian in the quotient; M_t rescales its graded coordinates and is core-equivariant.
transition_maps.justification: M_t is additive and integer-lattice preserving for integer t. It need not be invertible.

consumed_object_identity.required: A top character descends only if it vanishes on the bad top ideal.
consumed_object_identity.constructed: The local descent lemma is conditional on real eta=0 on the specified top words.
consumed_object_identity.justification: This node does not prove the analytic annihilation. The actual supplied vanishings come later from Section9–11.

coefficient_conventions.required: Integral characters, real spans and lattices must not be interchanged.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: Hall integral coordinates establish the lattice condition; real vanishing establishes descent.
coefficient_conventions.justification: The construction does not infer real vanishing merely from integrality or a discrete restriction.

local_conditions.required: The global unit test must exist for an integral top torus character.
local_conditions.constructed: Finitely many local torus sections and a squares partition produce a finite-dimensional smooth unit function.
local_conditions.justification: The sections and partition are fixed for the compact geometry, and bounds depend on that geometry and character.

exceptional_cases.required: Zero or negative petal multipliers and noncentral kernels are allowed.
exceptional_cases.constructed: Additive M_t and normal quotient construction include these cases.
exceptional_cases.justification: No inverse to M_t and no centrality of the bad-word kernel is assumed.

downstream_consumption.required: Section9–11 needs the algebraic model before proving actual vanishings; LP04 needs descent afterwards.
downstream_consumption.constructed: The algebraic model and conditional descent are available without the analytic premise.
downstream_consumption.justification: The actual eta descent and comparison are supplied by the distinct GI-08-LP04 node after Section9–11.

source_hypotheses.required: Actual Section9–11 real bad-word annihilation, a taut degree-rank model, strictly lower degree-rank auxiliary geometry and matching horizontal Taylor classes.
source_hypotheses.constructed: The construction applies the Hall quotient to that character and those represented families.
source_hypotheses.justification: It consumes actual analytic vanishings from GI-07-S9-11; the algebraic conditional lemma is insufficient by itself.

constructed_objects.required: Construct one common lower-rank model for the entire tensor chi tensor conjugate zeta.
constructed_objects.constructed: Successor groups J_i and diagonal lifts D(U_i) form H_i; the top is D(T).
constructed_objects.justification: LP13 rational generated-subgroup and central-quotient geometry applies to the constructed groups and lattice.

index_domain_coverage.required: The equality must hold at all limit points and all required n.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: Strong global unit tests, normalized polynomial orbits and the exact triple polynomial are used.
index_domain_coverage.justification: The vertical phases cancel on the full top subgroup, so the whole test descends, not just one component or one scalar projection.

transition_maps.required: Horizontal torus matching must lift to the correct common model.
transition_maps.constructed: Bounded normalization and lattice-class lifts give the diagonal comparison polynomial.
transition_maps.justification: GTZ B9 and B4 apply to the actual filtered source and target. Tautification occurs before the comparison.

consumed_object_identity.required: Downstream rank iteration consumes the full tensor matrix.
consumed_object_identity.constructed: Every coordinate of chi tensor conjugate zeta lies on the same lower-rank quotient.
consumed_object_identity.justification: The quotient equality identifies the actual input and output represented sequences; selecting a nonzero component would not suffice.

coefficient_conventions.required: Lower rank and lower ordinary degree differ.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: The result has degree-rank at most (m,R-1).
coefficient_conventions.justification: Only R=1 gives ordinary degree at most m-1. Bounds are for fixed m,R, dimensions and character, not unbounded character complexity.

local_conditions.required: All local lifts and test bounds must be standard and uniform over the family.
local_conditions.constructed: Fixed finite charts and bounded normalization provide common geometric and Lipschitz bounds.
local_conditions.justification: Polynomial coefficients and interval length do not enter the chosen finite geometry.

exceptional_cases.required: Components may vanish and old tests need not already be equivariant for the full ordinary top.
exceptional_cases.constructed: The full matrix argument permits zero components.
exceptional_cases.justification: The later S12 ordinary-top extension chooses a new compatible test before this comparison; unit completion alone is not that extension.

downstream_consumption.required: S12 and rank restart need the same tensor and a global padded output.
downstream_consumption.constructed: This node supplies the lower-rank tensor once its actual input test is fixed.
downstream_consumption.justification: S12 supplies the global multidegree output and fixed isometry; RANK removes incoming padding on the first tensor factor only.

source_hypotheses.required: The actual Section9–11 family has form g0 M_{fractional(alpha h)} g1 in the LP04 quotient.
source_hypotheses.constructed: Core data are independent of h, with fixed rational Hall geometry and abelian petal groups.
source_hypotheses.justification: The construction uses the ordered actual family, not merely scalar matching data.

constructed_objects.required: Construct a global unit multidegree (1,m) output equal to a fixed padding of zeta_h.
constructed_objects.constructed: The explicit K law, additive shear rho and right semidirect H law produce the two-variable model.
constructed_objects.justification: The full Lie bidegree filtration includes H_(0,1), H_(1,0) and the central H_(1,m), with an explicit integer lattice.

index_domain_coverage.required: Cover all integer inputs before transferring to limit inputs.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: The actual Z^2 source and target filtrations are checked before GTZ B4 is applied.
index_domain_coverage.justification: Binomial formulas include negative increments, and exact lattice right multiplication reduces alpha h. Fixed charts cover every box and retain a positive-density subfamily.

transition_maps.required: Extend the top character integrally before comparison.
transition_maps.constructed: The Hall basis extends eta from rank top T to ordinary G_m; a new G_m-equivariant unit test is chosen.
transition_maps.justification: Its restriction to T is the original character, so the actual LP04 comparison can be applied to this chosen test. An arbitrary old T-test is not silently upgraded.

consumed_object_identity.required: Recover the same zeta_h with fixed zero padding.
consumed_object_identity.constructed: Finite chart tests and global same-frequency unit completion give Z(h,n)=I zeta_h(n).
consumed_object_identity.justification: The inclusion I is fixed. Combining with the entire LP04 matrix uses a fixed unit contraction with no component division.

coefficient_conventions.required: Respect left/right conventions and avoid treating M_t as an automorphism.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: The additive shear rho is invertible; M_t need not be.
coefficient_conventions.justification: The specified right H law and right lattice reduction give the polynomial identity; reversing them changes the sequence.

local_conditions.required: The number of charts, target class and Lipschitz bounds must be independent of coefficients.
local_conditions.constructed: A fixed finite positive-margin cover and partition give density at least a standard reciprocal chart number.
local_conditions.justification: Target class is at most m+1 and bounds depend on the fixed source geometry, not h or N.

exceptional_cases.required: Empty petal families, trivial top and zero character must be included.
exceptional_cases.constructed: The formulas specialize to trivial rescalings and trivial torus functions in those cases.
exceptional_cases.justification: Global transfer uses standard constructions and exact all-limit identities; zero padding does not create new nonvanishing assumptions.

downstream_consumption.required: Rank iteration needs full lower-rank matrix and the exact global padded output.
downstream_consumption.constructed: This construction supplies the latter and selects the ordinary-top test used by LP04 for the former.
downstream_consumption.justification: It does not assert ordinary degree lowering at R>1. The combined join is consumed anew at each rank restart.

sections.title: ## Inputs and their identities
sections.claim_text:
Retain the original surface A/K and its base change to L from the first height proof. The normalized-cover construction supplies K/Q normal of degree at most F0, T=S union supp(M), and good reduction of A outside places over S. Here M=M_S(u) is the positive squarefree product in the manuscript; the empty product is one. The full-endomorphism-field construction supplies L/Q normal, d=[L:Q]<=D, unramified outside T. These are genuine incoming geometric inputs, not consequences of this quantitative argument.

Retain the actual normalized maps a_sigma mu_sigma, the sign cochain beta, and the original matrix-unit factors r_ell. The current A007 construction gives beta squared equal to chi, its prescribed sign coboundary, and after the quadratic correction a conjugation-invariant character beta|G_L. Its kernel defines the actual L-prime. On G_L the inflated maps and positive normalization scalars are identities. The original family is unramified outside T union {ell}. The accepted beta all-prime comparison identifies these same r_ell with the realizations of the same final primitive weight-two form f; direct Carayol then identifies their local Artin conductor with the primitive-level exponent when ell differs from the residue characteristic.

Use exactly the manuscript constants

    G0 = 116064000000,
    E0 = 10(D G0)^2,
    U0 = 4(D G0)^2,
    Q = R^(R E0),
    R >= max(D, max(S), 10^12).

No auxiliary comparison field replaces L or L-prime, and no degree of such a field enters these constants.

sections.title: ## The actual kernel degree
sections.claim_text:
The selected local characters give m=order(chi)<=2 R^R M. Indeed their order divides the least common multiple of the selected orders, hence at most twice the product of p-1 over the selected odd primes in T. The factors at p<=R contribute at most R^R; those at p>R contribute at most M, because every such prime of T lies in supp(M).

The corrected beta still takes values in mu_(2m), so

    d-prime = [L-prime:Q] <= 2m d <= 4 R^(R+1) M <= Q M.

For the final inequality, R>=10^12 implies 4<=R, and E0>=10 implies R+2<=R E0. Thus 4 R^(R+1)<=R^(R+2)<=R^(R E0). This uses the actual kernel field and preserves the first family's m bound. It is not the separate b-family bound 2304R. Also Q>=10^12 and M>=1.

sections.title: ## The retained local ramification calculation
sections.claim_text:
The detailed derivative and subgroup calculation is already independently checked in the A012 section of the 2026-11-05 galois-height REPORT and in the independent A012-SECOND-REVIEW. Those reports identify the inspected source as Serre, Local Class Field Theory, Chapter VI in Cassels--Frohlich, sections4.1--4.3, printed155--159, not the uninspected Local Fields book. Their substantive calculation is retained here.

For an extension of Q_p of degree at most a, its normal closure has degree at most a!. Over the maximal unramified subfield of that closure, an Eisenstein polynomial f of degree e for a uniformizer has derivative terms with distinct valuations modulo e. Consequently there is no cancellation at the minimum and v(f'(pi))<=e-1+e v_p(e). The derivative product over inertia conjugates and the lower-group definition give d_diff=sum_(i>=0)(|G_i|-1). Changing variables with the Herbrand function gives

    d_diff/e = 1-1/e + integral_(u>0)(1-1/|G^u|) du.

Before the last positive upper break the integrand is at least one half. The last break is therefore at most 2(1+log_2(a!))<=4a^2. The unramified and tame cases satisfy the same bound. For a Galois subfield F/Q_p, the exact subgroup rule is G_Qp^u intersect G_F = G_F^(psi_F/Qp(u)), with psi(u)>=u for u>=0. The inverse Herbrand function, not phi, is used. The two cited independent reports give the derivative proof of this indexing identity and the normal-closure justification.

At any p put F=L_v. Adjoin A[3], except at p=3 adjoin A[5]. The degree over Q_p is at most D G0: G0=|GL4(F5)| dominates |GL4(F3)|. Silverberg--Zarhin1995 Theorem3.5, printed406, has n>=3 and n prime to p; over F(A[n]) its required unramified torsion premise is satisfied by the identity extension. The A013 acceptance checks this exact scan and the semistability hypothesis. Pass to a normal closure if necessary. For ell different from p, semistability makes inertia unipotent. A stable ell-adic lattice shows that the pro-p wild image is finite, since the congruence kernel is pro-ell; a finite unipotent subgroup in characteristic zero is trivial. Thus absolute upper groups with u>U0 act trivially on V_ell(A) and lie in G_L.

On those groups the a_sigma mu_sigma factor is one. For odd p, chi is tame; beta squared is chi, so beta on wild pro-p inertia has order dividing two and is trivial. At p=2 the non-2 Dirichlet factors of chi are unramified and its possible factor modulo4 has order at most two on Q_2-units. Local reciprocity's norm compatibility gives chi|G_F(x)=chi(N_F/Q2(x)); apply it to the finite cyclic character field cut out by local chi. The retained norm-functoriality locator is Milne, Class Field Theory, v4.03, V Proposition3.3, printed157. Norms of units are units. Hence beta^4=chi^2=1 on O_F^*. This uses the finite-abelian norm functoriality itself, not only a quadratic example of it.

Write e=v_F(2)<=D. Logarithm and exponential are inverse on U_F^(e+1) and the ideal m_F^(e+1); the nonlinear series terms have strictly larger valuation there. Multiplication by four gives

    (U_F^(e+1))^4 = U_F^(3e+1).

Thus beta is trivial on U_F^(3e+1), its relative last upper break is at most 3e, and the subgroup rule makes it trivial on absolute upper groups above max(4D^2,3e)<=U0. This is the actual beta character over F, not a bound obtained from [L-prime:Q].

The two-dimensional r_ell therefore has tame invariant codimension at most two and Swan conductor at most 2U0. Possible infinite tame unipotent monodromy does not alter this wild integral. For every p and ell different from p,

    a_p(r_ell) <= 2+2U0 <= E0.

sections.title: ## Large primes and the primitive level
sections.claim_text:
If p>R, then p is outside S, so the original A has good reduction at each place of L above p by base change from the supplied good-reduction model over K. Also [L_v:Q_p]<=D<p, so L_v/Q_p is tame. Absolute wild inertia lies in G_L, acts trivially on the good-reduction Tate module, and is killed by the odd-prime beta argument. Hence a_p(r_ell)<=2. Outside T the original normalized family is unramified, so its exponent is zero.

For each residue prime choose ell different from it. The accepted same-beta all-prime isomorphism and the separate direct Carayol theorem give a_p(r_ell)=v_p(N) for the same final primitive form f. This includes dyadic and bad primes. Since T=S union supp(M) and every prime in S is at most R,

    N <= product_(p<=R) p^E0 * product_(p>R,p|M) p^2
      <= R^(R E0) M^2 = Q M^2.

The bound for small primes uses at most R primes, each at most R. Including the small prime factors of M again in M squared only weakens the inequality. The auxiliary choice of ell and the finite set used for trace comparison do not enlarge T.

sections.title: ## Fixed polarized point and coordinate
sections.claim_text:
Use B=(2,-3), O=Z[i,(1+j)/2], mu=2j+ij and E(x,y)=Trd(mu^-1 x bar(y)). The displayed integral matrix on the actual rank-four order has determinant one. The positive sign and Rosati involution match the principal polarized moduli problem. The printed Baba–Granath form is 6E; it is not called principal here. The accepted A001 proof explains why preservation of E and 6E gives the same isomorphism relation while the actual object uses E.

For this discriminant-six datum the twisting involutions generate the full four-element positive-normalizer quotient. The three distinct rational marked points have branch orders 4,6,2 and CM discriminants -4,-3,-24. The unique coordinate taking them to 0,infinity,-16/27 is the same coordinate as in the accepted Lin–Yang calculation. Its divisor identities and CM(-24) substitution give the weighted tuple [12(j+1),6(j^2+j+1),4(j^3-2j^2+1),j^3]. This uses the accepted corrected route, not the disputed product-isomorphism or explicit-conic argument. On the finite nonzero j locus it identifies the same principally polarized coarse point.

sections.title: ## Actual full-three cover and universal object
sections.claim_text:
The B11 construction begins with the admissible V1(5) fine model over Z[1/30], refines the five-marking, and adds the full three-marking. The division-lattice argument gives a free rank-one O3 module, including the ramified prime3; full-three marking is not imported from a theorem requiring the marking level prime to6. The five-marking action is free: a polarized automorphism has finite order, is congruent to1 on T3, and hence is1 by the torsion-free congruence argument and faithful Tate action.

The accepted corrected quotient/descent provider proves projectivity with the quasi-compact, quasi-separated affine terminal base and supplies effective descent of the abelian scheme and its actual maps. Its ample-sheaf norm is used for projectivity, not as a replacement polarization. Thus the degree-one polarization, O-action and three-marking descend unchanged. Arbitrary full-three objects acquire five-markings by the split-five matrix-unit argument, so the quotient represents the full functor, including every determinant component.

The separate generic-functor proof identifies this actual quotient and family with the full adelic Y3 over Q. It uses inverse frames and the matching canonical right action, an actual Q-map into a fine Siegel model, and faithful-flat descent; it does not descend an arbitrary complex isomorphism. The temporary five level is forgotten. The normalizer index on this identified whole curve is at most 4*3^4=324. Its central-idele cancellation and two ramified parity factors retain all components. Consequently the same forgetful j map has total degree at most324. The initially conditional assembly decision is consumed together with its accepted provider update and generic identification, never alone as full B11 acceptance.

sections.title: ## Tame pullback and the field
sections.claim_text:
Each component has genus at least2. For p>324 the finite action extends to the smooth proper model and is tame. A nontrivial prime-to-p finite-order automorphism cannot specialize to the identity. At a fixed point its tangent character is faithful, so the stabilizer is cyclic; its fixed point has a unique Hensel lift. These facts exclude new branch orbits or collisions. The quotient retains the three disjoint ordered sections and branch indices4,6,2. Their unique normalized coordinate is the given j, without discarding extra denominator primes.

Pull back by J(u)=-57600F(u)^2/G(u)^6. The identity G^6-97200F^2=H^2 gives pullback multiplicities2,6,2; tame normalization leaves indices2,1,1. The discriminants and resultants have prime support at most13. The normalized cover therefore has degree at most324, is branched only at the six contacts, and locally has u-c=z^2 after unramified extension. Positive even contact valuation gives unramified specialization; negative valuation specializes at the unbranched infinity point. These are exactly the places encoded by M_S(u).

Since u is not a contact, its fiber is finite etale of degree at most324. Its splitting field K is normal over Q of degree at most324!, and the local calculation makes K unramified outside T=S union supp(M_S(u)). Choose a point of this fiber and pull back the universal abelian scheme to obtain the actual principally polarized O-surface A/K. The proper model and universal abelian scheme give good reduction at every place not over S, including places over supp(M_S(u)). This is stronger than merely excluding T from the good-reduction statement.

Every conjugate has the same rational j=J(u), finite and nonzero: F(u) is nonzero and G has negative discriminant. The accepted polarized coarse relation and weighted tuple identify the same geometric polarized moduli point. They do not assert a universal family on the coarse line. This supplies exactly the original A/K and common-point input for the H6 Weil-restriction/ordered-Hom proof, and the same principal point and coordinate required by the theta comparison.

sections.title: ## Precise algebraic statement
sections.claim_text:
Let A be an abelian surface over an algebraic closure of a characteristic-zero field. Suppose quasi-isogenies mu_sigma: sigma A -> A satisfy

    mu_sigma o sigma(mu_tau) = c(sigma,tau) mu_sigma_tau,

where c(sigma,tau) belongs to Q*. The rationality of this discrepancy is an input. It does not follow from the dimension of A alone. In particular it must be checked against the actual endomorphism algebra and chosen equivariance condition.

Use the usual degree of a genuine isogeny. The external input is Milne, Abelian Varieties, Arithmetic Geometry, Springer, 1986, Theorem 8.2 and its preceding paragraph, printed p. 115, with proof on p. 116: deg([n]_A)=n^(2 dim A), hence n^4 here, and multiplicativity of degree. The degree is the rank of a finite locally free map, which is unchanged under field conjugation. For negative n use the degree-one automorphism [-1]. The actual published pages were visually checked; their exact image hashes are in SOURCE-ATTACHMENT.md.

For a quasi-isogeny u define D(u)=deg([m]u)/m^4, where m is any positive integer clearing its denominators. This is independent of m. Indeed, if m and n both clear the denominators, then

    deg([n]([m]u)) = n^4 deg([m]u)
    deg([m]([n]u)) = m^4 deg([n]u),

and the two maps coincide. Thus their degrees coincide and the two quotients agree. A common denominator proves D(uv)=D(u)D(v), and conjugating an integral representative proves D(sigma u)=D(u). Also D(id)=1, so D(u^-1)=D(u)^-1.

For c=a/b in Q*, with a a nonzero integer and b a positive integer, use a denominator divisible by b and the multiplication-degree theorem to obtain

    D(cu)=c^4 D(u).

No degree is being assigned directly to a nonexistent algebraic morphism [1/b]. This formula uses the preceding definition on rational quasi-isogenies.

Set d_sigma=D(mu_sigma)^(1/4), choosing the positive real fourth root. These are positive real algebraic numbers. The discrepancy identity gives

    d_sigma d_tau = |c(sigma,tau)| d_sigma_tau.

Consequently its normalized scalar cocycle is

    epsilon(sigma,tau)
      = c(sigma,tau) d_sigma_tau / (d_sigma d_tau)
      = c(sigma,tau)/|c(sigma,tau)| in {+1,-1}.

Equivalently nu_sigma=d_sigma^-1 mu_sigma satisfies nu_sigma sigma(nu_tau)=epsilon(sigma,tau)nu_sigma_tau after extending the rational Hom spaces by real algebraic scalar coefficients, with trivial Galois action on this auxiliary coefficient field. The normalized nu_sigma are formal scalar-extended homomorphisms; the argument does not assert that they remain algebraic quasi-isogenies. One can avoid this notation entirely and use the displayed scalar cocycle formula. The cocycle identity follows by multiplying the original cocycle by the coboundary of d^-1. Positivity removes the fourth-root ambiguity.

sections.title: ## Separate finite-cochain obligation
sections.claim_text: This calculation proves that epsilon is sign-valued. It does not prove that its class is zero, produce a splitting cochain, or imply that a splitting cochain has finite image. If a later construction requires such a cochain, its domain, continuity, coefficient action and splitting theorem must be supplied separately. Sign-valued cocycles need not be coboundaries on an arbitrary fixed finite quotient. Likewise continuity or finite image of d requires the corresponding property of the chosen mu_sigma family; it is not a consequence of pointwise degree normalization.

sections.title: ## Conductor bridge, conditional on the actual representations
sections.claim_text:
Fix a rational prime p and choose an auxiliary prime ell different from p. Suppose the actual geometric and modular two-dimensional ell-adic representations in one specified family are isomorphic as G_Q representations. Restriction gives an isomorphism on a decomposition group at p and on every inertia and ramification subgroup. The dimensions of inertia-invariants agree, as do all terms defining the Swan conductor. Therefore their Artin conductor exponents agree. This argument works separately for each constructed family; an isomorphism or endomorphism calculation for the b-family does not supply the beta-family premise.

An independent local compatibility/conductor theorem must identify the modular representation exponent with v_p(N_f), where N_f is the primitive newform's level. That theorem must cover p dividing N_f and the actual coefficient embedding. The Tate-module identification alone does not supply this assertion. A fixed auxiliary prime ell=3 cannot be used for this argument at p=3. To state a product conductor formula for a larger Tate module, the direct-sum multiplicities and coefficient-field degrees must also be checked explicitly.

sections.title: ## A055 source
sections.claim_text: Matiyasevich, Diophantine representation of enumerable predicates, Mathematics of the USSR-Izvestiya 5 (1971), printed p.2, explicitly invokes Lagrange: every nonnegative integer is a sum of four integer squares. Exact original PDF SHA256 18e824c01046ad49b079f91b567b27a928e737c598eb347c8a4f42128081ec83. The page was visually read. Its subsequent positive-natural convention uses +1; the current manuscript instead uses nonnegative indices and therefore no +1. Only the four-square assertion is imported.

sections.title: ## A055 rational connection
sections.claim_text: For rational s>0 write 1/s=a/b with positive integers a,b. Choose integers u_i with sum u_i^2=ab and put z_i=u_i/b. Then s sum z_i^2=1. Conversely this equation implies sum z_i^2>0 and s>0 in Q. Every nonnegative rational a is a sum of four rational squares by the same denominator clearing (zero uses four zeroes). Thus a=sum z_i^2 and a^2=x^2 holds precisely for a=|x|. These assertions concern rational witnesses and do not assert their integrality. They supply current lines258–269.

sections.title: ## A055 natural-index connection
sections.claim_text: At current lines437–442 multiplication first enforces membership on all three point-code roots. Hence in its four square calls the four initially untyped roots have codes iota(n_i) for integers n_i, and the outputs have codes iota(n_i^2), by the separate multiplication soundness contract. Canonical-input addition then produces iota(sum n_i^2). Conversely for every n>=0 Lagrange supplies integer n_i; multiplication completeness and canonical addition completeness supply all witnesses. Consequently this predicate defines exactly iota(Z_{>=0}). The separate membership/multiplication/addition contracts, including all-input typing and the established integer-index carrier, are premises here. Generator existence alone does not prove multiplication completeness. There is no circular use of this natural predicate to establish multiplication.

sections.title: ## A056 source
sections.claim_text: Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, second edition2009, ExerciseIII.3.7 pp105–106: for a nonsingular short Weierstrass model, the positive-index division polynomials have the stated parity and recurrences; parts(c),(d),(f) give coprimality, scalar coordinates and zeros exactly at nonidentity n-torsion. Exact published PDF SHA256 72ee67bfa1e3fdf582ac7e4b032d7ca0b35a168ed6443ac39c121fbb788cab25. The official2011 errata p4 corrects the omega numerator to a minus sign (PDF SHA256 cc89fd821b15df1fa2e139d32dbee447793ffc004fcf4f7cd962191873a2c37a). The retained2022 errata corrects the even parity factor and requests explicit small-index conventions; here psi0=0, psi(-1)=-1 and n=1,2 are checked from the bases. These are published exercise statements with official corrections; no claim is made that the exercise solutions are printed. The former Sutherland lecture-note supplier is retained only as historical provenance.

The displayed omega numerator has a minus sign. Exact PDF SHA256 4d638ce3bbe1127ae7947a8b4deda6c6e51247912194bbacaf3920d4c9bb19d7. This is an author lecture note, not a peer-reviewed article. We use its stated theorem.

sections.title: ## A056 normalization and guards
sections.claim_text: Work first in the generic coordinate ring y^2=x^3+Ax, and then specialize to the nonsingular fixed curve A=-d^2 over K0. Set psi_n=f_n for odd n and psi_n=2y f_n for even n. The initial values are f_0=0, f_1=f_2=1, f_3=3x^4+6Ax^2-A^2 and f_4=2(x^6+5Ax^4-5A^2x^2-A^3). The odd recurrence yields D0 L-R when m is even and L-D0 R when m is odd, where D0=(2y)^4=16(x^3+Ax)^2, L=f_{m+2}f_m^3, R=f_{m-1}f_{m+1}^3. The even recurrence cancels the even-index factors and gives f_{2m}=f_m(f_{m+2}f_{m-1}^2-f_{m-2}f_{m+1}^2) for m>=3; smaller indices are the bases. Every recursive index is smaller than the index being defined. The cancellations are polynomial identities before specialization, not division by an ordinate that might vanish.

sections.title: ## A056 exact scalar connection
sections.claim_text: The corrected omega_n=(psi_{n+2}psi_{n-1}^2-psi_{n-2}psi_{n+1}^2)/(4y) and the even recurrence give psi_{2n}=2psi_n omega_n; n=1,2 follow from the bases. Therefore 2y([n]P)psi_n(P)^4=psi_{2n}(P), while x([n]P)psi_n(P)^2=phi_n(P). For a nonidentity point P in the torsion-free carrier and n!=0, [n]P is not the identity, so psi_n(P)!=0 by ExerciseIII.3.7(f), with coprimality supplied separately by part(c). With this guard, the two cleared equations uniquely recover both coordinates of [n]P. The inverse-norm guard is the separately supplied field encoding of nonzero elements of K0; it is not established by division polynomials. n=0 and identity P use their explicit identity branches. Negative n uses psi_{-n}=-psi_n and group negation, preserving the ordinate sign. This supplies current278–304 and its actual scalar-template use. The pinned official errata and published exercise now replace the Sutherland source; the earlier access limitation is historical. Existing finite scalar tests are supplementary checks, not the proof.

Therefore 2y([n]P)psi_n(P)^4=psi_{2n}(P), while x([n]P)psi_n(P)^2=phi_n(P). For a nonidentity point P in the torsion-free carrier and n!=0, [n]P is not the identity, so psi_n(P)!=0 by the scalar-coordinate theorem and coprimality. With this guard, the two cleared equations uniquely recover both coordinates of [n]P. sections.title: ## A057 source and fixed-catalogue connection
sections.claim_text: For every fixed integer q>=3 and gcd(a,q)=1, the published Bennett–Martin–O'Bryant–Rechnitzer estimate gives theta(x;q,a)=x/phi(q)+O_q(x/log x). The exact source and the deduction of infinitude are supplied in ../prime-realization-current/SOURCE.md, lines3–4. In current306–308 the fixed integer W=4 product_{p<=324}p is at least4, so this estimate applies to every unit class modulo W. Choosing log x greater than twice the fixed implied constant times phi(W) makes theta(x;W,a) at least x/(2phi(W)), which is unbounded. Thus each such class contains infinitely many primes; deleting primes<=324 leaves infinitely many. Ascending enumeration with finite trial primality and congruence tests therefore stops after finding22 primes in each of the finitely many unit classes. The union is the fixed finite catalogue H_cat and defines N_s exactly as before. This proves only termination of this catalogue; it gives no asserted effective largest-prime bound and does not establish the separate M0 index.
sections.prior_claim_text: Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03 (6August2020), ChapterV Theorem2.2, printed p.155: for every positive integer modulus m and every a coprime to m the rational primes congruent to a modulo m have Dirichlet density 1/phi(m), hence infinitely many. Exact PDF SHA256 50d79af78250a9f1117ad9d337e0b231704a533fc707966ed1bfa52e13d498f5; this is an author course note. In current306–308 set the fixed positive integer W=4 product_{p<=324}p. There are finitely many unit classes a modulo W. Each has infinitely many primes, and deleting the finite set <=324 leaves infinitely many. Ascending enumeration with finite trial primality tests and a congruence test therefore stops after finding22 in each class. The union is a fixed finite catalogue H_cat; its product with product_{p<=324}p defines N_s. This proves termination of this particular catalogue only, with no effective bound on its final prime and no claim about every later prime choice. The successful M0 index and its proof are separate.

sections.title: ## A058 class and unit sources
sections.claim_text: For K0=Q(s), s^2=2, the direct proof in ../qroot2-class-units-current/PROOF.md shows O_K0=Z[s] by trace/norm parity, and discriminant8. Nearest-integer rounding in both coefficients gives Euclidean remainder norm at most one half of the divisor norm, so every ideal is principal. Reducing a unit positive at the real embedding s>0 by powers of epsilon=1+s into [1,epsilon) forces its s coefficient to be zero; consequently all units are uniquely +/-epsilon^k. Thus units modulo squares have four classes, and the independent sign vectors of -1 and epsilon distinguish them. Every totally positive unit is a square. This replaces the general course-note Minkowski and unit-rank inputs only for this fixed field, and supplies current344–346. Rank, torsion, descent and saturation remain separate.
sections.prior_claim_text: Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08 (19July2020), Theorem4.3 printed p.70 and Theorem5.1 printed p.85: every ideal class has an integral representative with norm at most (n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrt(|disc K|); the unit group of a number field is finitely generated with rank r1+r2-1 and torsion its roots of unity. Exact PDF SHA256 de2066ee7a319c0e6e521895a7e9e9567c2804bcafc0c8e67c417e508f2bc26b; these are author course notes. For K0=Q(s), s^2=2, its integral basis1,s gives discriminant8 and two real places. Minkowski bound is sqrt2<2, so the representative has norm1 and every ideal class is trivial. Roots of unity in a real field are +/-1, hence the units modulo squares have order4. The sign vectors of -1 and epsilon=1+s are independent, so this sign map on the four squareclasses is bijective and a totally positive unit is a square. This supplies current344–346. It does not claim epsilon is a chosen fundamental unit.

sections.title: ## A058 two-isogeny source
sections.claim_text: Silverman, Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, second edition2009, ChapterX Example4.8 printed p.336 and its connecting-homomorphism calculation continuing p.337 give the x-squareclass connecting map for a rational two-isogeny, with identity value1 and kernel-point value given by the linear coefficient. Exact PDF SHA256 72ee67bfa1e3fdf582ac7e4b032d7ca0b35a168ed6443ac39c121fbb788cab25. The displayed curve in Proposition4.9 p.337 misprints a^2-b for a^2-4b; we do not use that misprinted equation. The printed isogeny ordinate has the opposite sign from our convention, which leaves its image and kernel unchanged. The following explicit computation fixes the exact convention.

sections.title: ## A058 explicit kernel connection
sections.claim_text: For E_b:y^2=x^3+bx, b!=0 in characteristic0, set phi(x,y)=(x+b/x,y(1-b/x^2)) on nonzero x, and hatphi(X,Y)=((X-4b/X)/4,Y(1+4b/X^2)/8) on E_{-4b}. Substitution verifies the equations; the maps extend across their poles, send identity to identity, have kernels {O,(0,0)}, and hatphi phi=[2]. The last identity follows by the usual doubling formula, with x=(x^2-b)^2/(4x(x^2+b)) and ordinate sign fixed by the differential2. Define alpha_b(O)=1, alpha_b((0,0))=b, alpha_b(P)=x(P) modulo squares otherwise. The line-intersection equation gives product of three nonzero abscissas c^2, proving the homomorphism; tangents have repeated roots, a line through(0,0) gives x(P+(0,0))=b/x(P), and vertical pairs give a square. For Q=(X,Y), x(hatphi Q)=(Y/(2X))^2. Conversely if x(P)=u^2!=0, put v=y/u, X=2(x+v), Y=2uX. Since v^2=x^2+b and b!=0, X!=0; substitution gives Q on E_{-4b} and hatphi Q=P. If P=(0,0) and b is a square, Q=(2sqrt(b),0) is a lift; O lifts O. Thus ker(alpha_b)=hatphi(E_{-4b}(K)). Applying the same argument on the dual curve and scaling E_{16b} to E_b gives ker(alpha_{-4b})=phi(E_b(K)). These are the exact maps used in the local computation; no Selmer-group upper bound is silently identified with a rational-point image.

sections.title: ## A058 actual local descent
sections.claim_text: Set b=-d^2, d=75-53s with norm7. In the PID Z[s], (d) is a prime of norm7. For E the valuations of x away from(d) are even: if m=v(x) is odd, the unequal valuations3m and m of x^3 and -d^2x have an odd minimum, impossible for y^2. Consequently alpha(E) lies in the eight squareclasses generated by -1,epsilon,d. Rational two-torsion gives1,-1,d,-d. Since epsilon^4 d=delta=3-s, scaling (x,y) to(epsilon^4x,epsilon^6y) sends E to C:y^2=x^3-delta^2x. R=(epsilon,2s) lies on C by substitution and its squareclass is epsilon (the scale epsilon^4 is a square), so all eight classes occur. Independence follows from the d-valuation and the two independent unit signs.

sections.title: ## A058 dual and quotient
sections.claim_text: On E_{4d^2}, every nonzero x is positive at both real embeddings because y^2=x(x^2+4d^2). At primes other than(s),(d), the same odd-valuation argument applies. At(s), valuations of the two terms are3m and m+4; equality requires m=2, so odd m is impossible. At(d) they are3m and m+2; the only odd equality is m=1. Writing x=d u then gives y^2=d^3 u(u^2+4); an even valuation would require u^2=-4 modulo(d), impossible in F7 whose nonzero squares are1,2,4. Thus all valuations of x are even. The PID and total positivity make its squareclass trivial by the preceding unit result; the exceptional point(0,0) has class4d^2, also a square. Therefore alpha_{4d^2} is trivial, E_{4d^2}(K0)=phi E(K0), and ker(alpha_{-d^2})=hatphi phi E(K0)=2E(K0). Hence [E(K0):2E(K0)]=8. Equivalently the extra term in the two-isogeny quotient sequence vanishes: a nonkernel rational two-torsion point maps to the dual kernel. This supplies current348–362, not the independent full-torsion or height computation.

sections.title: ## A058 odd free index
sections.claim_text: Use the separately established rank1 and full rational two-torsion result for E, transported to C by the displayed isomorphism. Write the pulled-back R=mG+T with G a generator of the free quotient and T torsion. If m were even, the squareclass homomorphism would give alpha(R)=alpha(T), since alpha(2G)=1. But alpha(R)=epsilon has opposite real signs, whereas1,-1,d,-d have equal signs: d and its conjugate are positive since75>53sqrt2. Contradiction. Thus m is odd and nonzero. This proves the odd-index assertion at367–368 only; it does not show |m|=1. The separate height bound and finite enumeration still establish saturation.

sections.title: ## BASE-FORWARD
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, An inverse theorem for the Gowers U^3(G) norm; Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society51 (2008),73–153; Forward Theorem10.11 pp124–125, equations10.7 and10.9; Theorem2.7, Corollary10.6 and Proposition10.10 in its proof. December2023 author notice identifies the false general quadratic-extension proposition. BASE uses its independently reviewed H={0} finite-box replacement; no backward theorem or skew-iterate result is imported.

Available statement: The forward prime-cyclic bracket theorem supplies a bounded-frequency bracket quadratic on a proper progression containing a Bohr set, with a positive shifted correlation for each nonempty subset of that progression. Hypotheses: P>2 prime and a fixed sufficiently small positive U3 lower bound eta. Range: Prime cyclic groups and the forward implication only. Conventions: Centered fractional-part representatives and cyclic averages. Exceptions: The proof chain uses the affected quadratic-extension assertion; only its H={0} proper-progression use is repaired locally here. No unmodified general extension theorem is accepted.

Current connection (GI-01-BASE2, 01-gi-base2 lines42–111): BASE42–65 imports only the forward cyclic bracket conclusion. BASE76–111 proves the H={0} specialization needed in Proposition10.10 by constant finite-box second differences, including side lengths1 and2, and converts its coordinate polynomial with the independent frequency lifts. This replaces the failed general extension step in the forward proof. It does not import the converse, Theorem12.9, or the erroneous skew iterate.

Separate inputs: Local finite-box specialization BASE76–111; Remaining GTZ polynomial closure and interval normalization are the other worker's slice..

sections.title: ## BASE-BOHR
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, An inverse theorem for the Gowers U^3(G) norm; Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society51 (2008),73–153; Definition2.6 printed p84; Lemmas8.1–8.2 printed pp105–106; regular Bohr sets. December2023 author notice identifies the false general quadratic-extension proposition. BASE uses its independently reviewed H={0} finite-box replacement; no backward theorem or skew-iterate result is imported.

Available statement: A Bohr set has a radius-dependent positive density bound and a regular radius can be selected in a fixed comparable interval; at a regular radius, small relative radius changes change cardinality by O(d epsilon). Hypotheses: Fixed finite frequency set and admissible positive radius; regularity perturbation epsilon within its d-dependent range. Range: Finite abelian groups; radii and frequency count held fixed for the application. Conventions: Group cardinality normalization and the source Bohr distance to integers. Exceptions: Empty frequency set is the full group and is handled separately without division by d.

Current connection (GI-01-BASE2, 01-gi-base2 lines114–149): Choose a regular radius below the already supplied progression inclusion radius. Apply the forward correlation to that same Bohr subset. The displayed cutoff differs from its indicator only in the two-sided shell; choosing epsilon after b_star and d loses at most half the correlation. Density gives the positive cyclic lower bound. P alpha_j integral makes the product periodic. These smoothing/periodicity deductions are local, not extra claims of the Bohr lemma.

Separate inputs: BASE-FORWARD phase and subset correlation; Local cutoff construction; no universal cutoff derivative constant.

sections.title: ## DF-WEAK
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; One-variable Proposition9.2 pp522–523 with Theorem2.9 and Lemma6.7 pp501–502; GT14 pp1175–1176 preserves one-variable scope. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: In one parameter, failed quantitative total equidistribution admits the bounded horizontal-character obstruction and weak factorization construction of Proposition9.2; Lemma6.7 characterizes adapted polynomial maps by supported binomial coordinate coefficients. Hypotheses: Fixed dimension/degree, adapted rational Malcev basis, positive quantitative failure parameter with the basis rationality bound absorbed. Range: One variable only; the published2014 correction preserves this scope. Conventions: Binomial coefficients supported in G_r at degree r; real horizontal lift is used in the construction. Exceptions: No multi-parameter unequal-side theorem or single-scale equidistribution equivalence is imported; stronger local coefficient/real-kernel claims require the displayed argument.

Current connection (GI-05-DF, 05-gi-df lines104–180): DF113–131 extracts a standard discrepancy and normalizes g(0)=c lambda. The source obstruction is transferred from the witnessing dense progression by the independently accepted MF91–138 inverse-affine estimate, rather than an invalid bounded-height claim for O(N) offsets. DF133–178 splits supported coefficients into nearest-integer and small parts. Exact real horizontal zero, not merely circle zero, puts p in a connected proper kernel. Rational numerators may be unbounded. Local closure and right-period arguments are separately exposed.

Separate inputs: MF-AFFINE current MF91–138, accepted also for DF132–145; GTZ polynomial group closure; DF rational coordinate/period deductions.

sections.title: ## DF-COORDINATES
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; Lemmas A.2–A.3 pp526–528, Lemma6.7 pp501–502. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: For a fixed rational Malcev basis, first/second-kind coordinate changes, multiplication and inversion are fixed rational polynomial maps. Hypotheses: A rational Malcev basis for the fixed nilpotent group and its lattice. Range: Fixed finite dimension and nilpotency step. Conventions: GT12 Lemmas A.2–A.3 coordinate conventions; right lattice quotient. Exceptions: These polynomial laws alone do not assert small Taylor bounds, a period, or all-cover equidistribution.

Current connection (GI-05-DF, 05-gi-df lines181–260): DF192–216 scales n=Nt and applies the fixed coordinate polynomials. Triangular monomial/binomial conversion preserves O(N^-r); the formal-weight Taylor extraction, using the separately supplied group-Taylor convention, rules out lower-weight contributions. Bounded derivatives on the fixed compact scaled range give O(1/N). DF218–259 also uses these same rational laws to construct the weighted denominator lattice and the right-difference polynomial. The latter is a local replacement for the flawed left-coset inference in A.12, not an unmodified application of its proof.

Separate inputs: GTZ B9 group Taylor convention; DF218–259 local overgroup and right-period proof, separately accepted root orientation002.

sections.title: ## DF-BSG-PLUNNECKE
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, An inverse theorem for the Gowers U^3(G) norm; Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society51 (2008),73–153; Theorems5.2–5.3, printed p95. December2023 author notice identifies the false general quadratic-extension proposition. BASE uses its independently reviewed H={0} finite-box replacement; no backward theorem or skew-iterate result is imported.

Available statement: A finite nonempty set with additive energy at least |A|^3/K has a large subset of bounded difference doubling; a finite set with difference doubling at most K has |kA-lA|<=K^(k+l)|A| for k,l>=1. Hypotheses: K>=1; high energy for Theorem5.2, bounded difference doubling for Theorem5.3. Range: Arbitrary additive groups as stated; applied here to a finite abelian product. Conventions: Energy counts ordered additive quadruples. Exceptions: No correlation premise or identification of the group with its dual is needed; Proposition5.4 is not used.

Current connection (GI-05-DF, 05-gi-df lines319–363): DF319–351 rounds into the actual product B x A with Q=100N+1 and M=ceil(1/e). The signed first coordinates and fixed target sum give a Fourier/Holder bound for the energy of any selected graph. Its size is at most3N and energy is bounded below by c2 N^3, so BSG applies with K depending only on c,C; Plunnecke with k=9,l=8 yields F2. Neither equal cyclic orders nor the specialized correlation premise of Proposition5.4 is assumed.

Separate inputs: Local rounding and Fourier/Holder energy calculation DF319–351; Later target-character separation DF364–396 is local, not a blind Lemma9.2 import.

sections.title: ## DF-BOHR-PROGRESSION
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, An inverse theorem for the Gowers U^3(G) norm; Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society51 (2008),73–153; Lemma6.4 pp97–98; Lemma10.4 and its lattice-lift proof p121 (using10.3). December2023 author notice identifies the false general quadratic-extension proposition. BASE uses its independently reviewed H={0} finite-box replacement; no backward theorem or skew-iterate result is imported.

Available statement: A positive-density subset of a finite additive group has a Bohr set B(S,1/4) in2A-2A with bounded |S|; a Bohr set contains a large proper coset progression whose real frequency generators are independent and add exactly in its lattice lift. Hypotheses: Positive density for Bogolyubov; finite frequency set and admissible positive radius for the progression construction. Range: Finite groups including composite cyclic groups. Conventions: The progression has exact lifted coordinates in the real frequency cube; the subgroup is the common annihilator. Exceptions: The subgroup need not vanish in general; that is obtained only after adding a faithful character in the current cyclic application.

Current connection (GI-05-DF, 05-gi-df lines364–433): The local separation argument DF364–396 constructs an exact Freiman map on2H_doubleprime-2H_doubleprime into the actual cyclic target, without identifying that target with the dual of B. Apply Bogolyubov to H_doubleprime in B=Z/Q. Add x/Q, making the annihilator zero, and take radius1/16. The source progression has independent real lifts. Delete inactive generators; centered coordinate paths stay in P, so local additivity integrates. Dual real vectors give F4. No quadratic extension or classification is imported.

Separate inputs: DF364–396 actual-target graph refinement; No GT08 Proposition3.2/10.7 use here.

sections.title: ## MF-EQUAL-CUBE
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, On the quantitative distribution of polynomial nilsequences—erratum; Annals of Mathematics 179 (2014),1175–1183; Corrected equal-side theorem, printed pp1176–1177; smoothness norm p1177; minor errata pp1182–1183. Final published erratum only; no unpublished arbitrary-side extension.

Available statement: On an equal cube [N]^t, a polynomial orbit in an m-dimensional rational filtered nilmanifold is delta-equidistributed or has a nonzero bounded horizontal character whose product-binomial C-infinity norm is bounded. Hypotheses: 0<delta<1/2; a 1/delta-rational adapted basis; integers m,t,N,d>=1. Range: Equal side lengths only; integer parameters >=1 visually verified on printed1176. Conventions: C-infinity norm is sup over alpha!=0 of N^|alpha| times the circle norm of the product-binomial coefficient. Exceptions: The original arbitrary-side theorem is not imported; zero-dimensional trivial groups are handled outside the failure case.

Current connection (GI-06-MF, 06-gi-multifactor lines139–173): MF147–161 subtracts the Haar mean, rotates to positive real discrepancy and tiles the dense progression index rectangle by equal cubes. Choose eta after discrepancy so discarded remainder is harmless. On the chosen cube apply exactly the published equal-side theorem, with error below both discrepancy and the reciprocal rationality bound. Finitely many bounded integer vectors make the character standard. MF-AFFINE, not the published unequal-side claim, transfers it to the original variables afterwards.

Separate inputs: MF91–138 inverse-affine transfer; Polynomial precomposition and support via GT12 Lemma6.7; Later factor construction not supplied by the obstruction theorem alone.

sections.title: ## MF-SUPPORTED-COEFFICIENTS
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; Lemma6.7 and Corollary6.8, pp501–502. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: Adapted polynomial maps have Malcev-coordinate binomial expansions whose coefficient at multiindex alpha is supported in the coordinates for filtration layer G_|alpha|, and the converse holds. Hypotheses: Fixed rational Malcev basis adapted to the finite-degree filtration. Range: Finite positive parameter count; total multiindex size, not the maximum coordinate index. Conventions: Product-binomial coefficients; the support is G_|alpha|. Exceptions: The characterization does not itself supply a horizontal obstruction or delete rational Taylor terms.

Current connection (GI-06-MF, 06-gi-multifactor lines175–198): MF175–190 normalizes the constant and uses the source support characterization to place t_alpha in G_|alpha|. The selected w_alpha,z_alpha remain in that coordinate subspace, so the converse characterization makes their maps polynomial. The real lift cancels exactly in the ordered middle factor, giving a connected real kernel. Closure under products is a separately registered GTZ input; the coordinate theorem alone is not asked to prove it.

Separate inputs: MF-EQUAL-CUBE obstruction; MF-AFFINE; GTZ polynomial group closure.

sections.title: ## MF-COORDINATES
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; Lemmas A.2–A.3 pp526–528, with Lemma6.7 coordinate degree. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: For a fixed rational Malcev basis, first/second-kind coordinate changes, multiplication and inversion are fixed rational polynomial maps. Hypotheses: A rational Malcev basis for the fixed nilpotent group and its lattice. Range: Fixed finite dimension and nilpotency step. Conventions: GT12 Lemmas A.2–A.3 coordinate conventions; right lattice quotient. Exceptions: These polynomial laws alone do not assert small Taylor bounds, a period, or all-cover equidistribution.

Current connection (GI-06-MF, 06-gi-multifactor lines201–250): MF202–225 applies rational polynomial laws to scaled variables and the separately supplied Taylor extraction. MF227–234 constructs the BCH-closed weighted denominator lattice. MF236–250 interpolates gamma on a fixed integer grid and forms the correctly ordered R_i. Since R_i(n,0)=0, every monomial contains r; a common denominator q makes each R_i(n,q) integral. This proves the right-coset period without the flawed orientation in the source A.12 proof. Least-dimension descent and common-core conclusions remain later local steps.

Separate inputs: GTZ B9 Taylor convention; MF weak factor construction; Local weighted denominator and right-period arguments.

sections.title: ## MF-LATTICE-LOGARITHMS
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; Definition2.1 and remarks p478; Lemma A.2 pp526–527. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: The ambient lattice has integer second-kind coordinates, and the change between first-kind logarithm coordinates and second-kind Malcev coordinates is a fixed rational polynomial map. Hypotheses: A connected simply connected nilpotent group with a rational Malcev basis relative to Gamma. Range: Fixed finite dimension and nilpotency step. Conventions: Definition2.1 integer second-kind lattice convention and Lemma A.2 coordinate conversion. Exceptions: The source only gives rational logarithm coordinates; Lie rationality from subgroup compactness remains the separate local argument.

Current connection (GI-06-MF, 06-gi-multifactor lines369–386): Definition2.1 makes lattice second-kind coordinates integers; A.2 therefore makes their logarithms rational. MF373–382 proves that their Lie span is the entire subgroup Lie algebra: a proper maximal nilpotent subalgebra would be a codimension-one ideal, yielding a surjection H->R that kills the lattice, contrary to compactness. Rational linear algebra identifies the intersection Lie algebra. The independent integration review checked this exact reverse direction; it is not a backward use of A.10.

Separate inputs: Given compact lattice quotients for P and G_d; Local maximal-subalgebra/compactness proof MF373–382.

sections.title: ## MF-INTERSECTION-LATTICE
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; Definitions2.1,2.3,2.5 pp478–480 and Proposition A.10 p534. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: A closed connected Lie-rational subgroup with a rational filtration admits a Malcev basis relative to its actual intersection with the ambient lattice. Hypotheses: GT12 Definition2.5 rational Lie basis with bounded rational height; ambient adapted rational basis; rational subgroup filtration. Range: Fixed finite dimension and step; a suitable finite rationality bound Q is chosen for the actual data. Conventions: Proposition A.10 supplies a basis for H/(H intersect Gamma); Definition2.1 identifies the associated integer coordinate lattice. Exceptions: Lie rationality is a premise and must be proved without assuming the desired compact quotient. Trivial subgroup is immediate.

Current connection (GI-06-MF, 06-gi-multifactor lines383–399): MF383–390 uses rational linear algebra and global exponential/BCH to obtain the exact closed connected K and rational lower-central filtration. Choose a finite standard Q for that actual data, apply A.10 and Definition2.1 to K intersect Gamma. MF392–394 injects its coset set into (P intersect Gamma)/Delta, proving finite index without normality. The later quotient uses this same K and the separately retained central-quotient lemma.

Separate inputs: MF-LATTICE-LOGARITHMS reverse rationality argument; LP13 central-quotient lemma; All-limit vertical identity for the actual vector.

sections.title: ## RANK-SUBGROUP-LATTICES
sections.claim_text:
Source: Green and Tao, The quantitative behaviour of polynomial orbits on nilmanifolds; Annals of Mathematics 175 (2012),465–540; Definitions2.1,2.3,2.5 pp478–480 and Proposition A.10 p534. Read with final2014 erratum: one-variable results retained, multiparameter application restricted to corrected equal-side theorem. Local right-period and affine repairs are kept distinct.

Available statement: A closed connected Lie-rational subgroup with a rational filtration admits a Malcev basis relative to its actual intersection with the ambient lattice. Hypotheses: GT12 Definition2.5 rational Lie basis with bounded rational height; ambient adapted rational basis; rational subgroup filtration. Range: Fixed finite dimension and step; a suitable finite rationality bound Q is chosen for the actual data. Conventions: Proposition A.10 supplies a basis for H/(H intersect Gamma); Definition2.1 identifies the associated integer coordinate lattice. Exceptions: Lie rationality is a premise and must be proved without assuming the desired compact quotient. Trivial subgroup is immediate.

Current connection (GI-10-RANK, 10-gi-rank lines59–73): RANK59–68 verifies rationality by rational brackets, the ideal property by weights, and closed connectedness by the exponential homeomorphism. Its rational lower-central layers and finite Q meet A.10. The supplied basis is relative to the actual lattice intersection, which is therefore discrete and cocompact. sections.title: ## CCL-NORMS
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: For compatible CM points on the source modular curve, the unaveraged conductor-raising trace is the Hecke operator at an inert new prime, and the Hecke operator minus the two prime Artin actions at a split new prime, with the stated unit factor.

Source/hypothesis scope: Source split-Heegner specialization N1=1; base conductor d prime to N; new prime outside6dND_K; O_K units exactly plus/minus1.

Needed current conclusion: For every actual old conductor d and permitted new prime, Tr(y_dell)=a_ell y_d when inert and Tr(y_dq)=(a_q-sigma_q-sigma_q^-1)y_d when split, with no conductor-dependent multiplier.

Connecting argument: Apply Theorem2.15 with source base conductor c=d and old multiplier m=1, not with d restricted to an inert squarefree product. N1=1 identifies the source curve with X0(N), and the unit quotient is1. The two split Artin elements multiply to the rational principal ideal(q), hence are inverses. Apply the fixed Hecke-equivariant elliptic quotient on degree-zero divisors. T_q[infinity]=(q+1)[infinity] cancels the degree correction. All sums remain unaveraged.

Separate inputs: Compatible CM points and orientations; Fixed normalized Hecke-equivariant elliptic quotient; Ordinary Artin reciprocity conventions.

sections.title: ## CUSP-MULTIPLIER
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: Every degree-zero cuspidal divisor class on the compactified modular curve of a congruence subgroup is torsion in its Jacobian.

Source/hypothesis scope: Fixed congruence subgroup Gamma0(N), all geometric cusps, and a fixed Q-defined homomorphism phi:J0(N)->E.

Needed current conclusion: A single positive C_pi depending only on fixed N and phi kills every cusp-convention translation; the good-prime norm has no cusp correction and pi(Wx)=w pi(x)+pi(W infinity).

Connecting argument: There are finitely many geometric cusps. Their degree-zero classes are torsion, so their finitely generated subgroup and its image under phi have finite exponent C_pi. This exponent kills the image over every field, without requiring individual cusps rational. The based Abel map and Hecke eigenquotient give the exact good-prime formula. For W, phi W_*=w phi gives pi(Wx)=w pi(x)+pi(W infinity), whose last term lies in the same finite image.

Separate inputs: Actual f-eigenquotient and Atkin-Lehner eigenvalue convention; Fixed curve and parametrization, not varying auxiliary levels.

sections.title: ## CM-CONGRUENCE
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: At an inert new prime prime to dN, the local CM order is the maximal unramified quadratic order. The CM curve has supersingular reduction, whose unique order-ell subgroup scheme is the relative Frobenius kernel; raising isogenies and prime-to-ell level structure specialize through it.

Source/hypothesis scope: Actual compatible CM points, inert ell outside dN, smooth good modular/elliptic models and extension of the fixed pi at ell.

Needed current conclusion: At a compatible place, reduction(y_dell)=F_ell reduction(y_d), with rational arithmetic Frobenius and the same identity after every old ideal-class translate, for arbitrary permitted old d.

Connecting argument: The local maximal order depends only on ell not dividing d. Each cyclic raising kernel closes to an order-ell subgroup and reduces to the unique Frobenius kernel, so every raising quotient reduces to the Frobenius quotient with the same prime-to-ell N-structure. Apply the integral extension of pi. Transport the chosen place with the ideal-class action. Howard section1.7 formula(13) is corroboration only on his restricted conductor family; his global descent and residual-surjectivity hypotheses are not imported.

Separate inputs: Classical CM moduli and supersingular subgroup facts as stated in the retained local proof; Good integral-model extension of pi; No arbitrary-conductor conclusion is taken from Howard.

sections.title: ## RELATIVE-DERIVATIVE
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: The ring-class Picard group is the finite-idelic double quotient by K* and the completed order units. For squarefree inert new primes, the relative local unit quotient is the product of F_(ell^2)^*/F_ell^*; the derivative operator satisfies (sigma_ell-1)D_ell=(ell+1)-Tr_ell.

Source/hypothesis scope: Imaginary quadratic K with units plus/minus1; f prime to the distinct new inert primes; compatible ring-class reciprocity; 2^a divides ell+1 and a_ell for each ell.

Needed current conclusion: The relative group Gal(H_fnI/H_f) is the product C_(ell+1), without an extra unit quotient, and delta_a(C_pi D_I y_fnI) is invariant under that whole relative group.

Connecting argument: Take the kernel of the order-class map in the idelic description and use Chinese remainders. The global units plus/minus1 already lie in every rational residue-unit denominator. The local factors are cyclic and commute. Telescope the finite sum defining D_ell. Apply the accepted inert norm relation; the difference under each generator is the Kummer class of an actual2^a multiple. Thus it vanishes and the class is invariant.

Separate inputs: Ring-class reciprocity/idelic class-group description; Accepted actual inert norm relation and Kummer functoriality.

sections.title: ## ONCE-UNTWISTED-DESCENT
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: For a closed normal subgroup H of a profinite group G and finite discrete continuous G-module V, inflation-restriction gives0->H1(G/H,V^H)->H1(G,V)->H1(H,V)^(G/H)->H2(G/H,V^H).

Source/hypothesis scope: G=G_Hf,H=G_MI,V=E[2^a] untwisted; the fixed2^e annihilates V^H; c is invariant under Gal(MI/Hf).

Needed current conclusion: There is a canonical additive transport- and coefficient-compatible operation d_a(c)=2^e b, with res(b)=2^e c and res(d_a(c))=2^(2e)c, using one multiplier for the whole extension and for I empty.

Connecting argument: The fixed2^e kills every cochain with values in V^H and hence both outside groups in the exact segment. Therefore2^e c lifts to b. Two lifts differ by the inflation image killed by2^e, so d_a(c) is independent of choice. Applying this uniqueness to sums and natural maps proves additivity and compatibility. Apply once to MI/Hf before any scalar or binary twist. For the trivial extension the same formula is2^(2e)c.

Separate inputs: Fixed uniform untwisted torsion exponent(H2), from the already supplied scalar construction; Invariant class from the previous derivative step; Later finite character construction and weighted push are separate.

sections.title: ## LANG-RESIDUE
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: For a connected algebraic group over a finite field, the Lang map is surjective; its first Galois cohomology over the finite field vanishes.

Source/hypothesis scope: The connected smooth special fiber of the Neron identity component over the finite residue field; finite unramified Fprime/F.

Needed current conclusion: H1(Gal(kprime/k), Bbar0(kprime))=0, so the residue of a cocycle in B0(Fprime) is a coboundary that can be lifted smoothly.

Connecting argument: Inflation-restriction injects the finite-residue-extension H1 into the zero finite-field H1. Equivalently, write the cyclic cocycle x=(F-1)y by Lang; its norm-zero equation gives(F^r-1)y=0, so y belongs to kprime. Smooth reduction lifts the cobounding point. No division by the extension degree occurs.

Separate inputs: Connected smooth Neron special fiber and surjectivity of smooth reduction.

sections.title: ## FORMAL-COHOMOLOGY
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: The formal group filtration has successive quotients identified additively with the corresponding residue-field ideal quotients; the kernel of reduction is the formal group, and reduction to nonsingular points gives the standard exact sequence.

Source/hypothesis scope: Finite unramified Fprime/F of nonarchimedean local fields; base uniformizer fixed by its finite Galois group; actual elliptic Neron/formal group.

Needed current conclusion: H1(Gal(Fprime/F),B0(Fprime))=0 and the geometric component order c_B kills H1(Gal(Fprime/F),B(Fprime)), including even extension degree.

Connecting argument: After the Lang step the cocycle lies in the formal group. Each quotient is the additive kprime module, induced by a normal basis, so positive cohomology vanishes. Successively correct the cocycle modulo increasing powers; completeness gives a limit, and finiteness of the group allows every cocycle equation to pass to the limit. The quotient B(Fprime)/B0(Fprime) embeds in the geometric component group, so its annihilator c_B kills the remaining H1 by the exact sequence.

Separate inputs: Previous Lang residue step; Normal-basis theorem and completeness; Geometric component group, not merely rational component count.

sections.title: ## FIXED-LOCAL-CONDITIONS
sections.claim_text:
Available statement: A class becoming Kummer after an unramified extension has image in H1(F,B) in the inflation-restriction kernel; this kernel is the image of H1(Gal(Fprime/F),B(Fprime)). The previous component-order bound annihilates it.

Source/hypothesis scope: Actual ring-class extensions unramified at2N and at good old places; K split at2N; finitely many fixed local quadratic types; previously constructed d_a and fixed C_pi,2^e.

Needed current conclusion: One fixed L=m0 C_pi C_bad2^(2e) gives b_Ia=m0 C_bad d_a(c_Ia) with restriction delta_a(L D_I y_fnI), old Kummer conditions, good odd unramified conditions, and full active/moving conditions, independently of K,f,I and coefficient dimensions.

Connecting argument: The Kummer exact sequence turns annihilation of the obstruction in H1(F,B) into Kummer membership over F. Geometric component groups are invariant under unramified base change, so one common multiple C_bad over the finitely many fixed types suffices. Combine the exact restriction formula for d_a with the initial C_pi. At a good odd place the formal kernel is uniquely2-divisible and finite-field Lang identifies the finite Kummer quotient with unramified H1, so the good condition is the unramified one. Full active/moving conditions impose no further restriction. m0 may be enlarged only by fixed multiplier requirements.

Separate inputs: Ring-class unramifiedness and fixed local types; Kummer exact sequence and preceding local cohomology bound; No weighted-character descent or later derivative identity is proved here.
